Fix: get each card from a real proposal, and add rows that confirm twice (already_done) and that cancel then confirm (already_cancelled), checking the outcome on each decided step.

auditArea reads only `audit.ok` and `trace.ok` from the cached chain walk. It cannot tell 'verified and intact' apart from 'never verified' or 'last check failed or is stale'. If the audit-check job hasn't run, or keeps failing, the hub shows the calm info chip ('N today') and no attention. A check that did not run reads as clear. The test table has no row for an unverified or stale status. Fix: pass the check's time or state into auditArea, and raise attention (for example 'not verified since …') when there is no verification or it is older than the check's schedule.

Class fix in the code, but no test proves it. `decide` now catches trace-write failures on the already_done, already_cancelled, needs_secret and expired paths, and keeps `run` fail-closed. The review-052 table only checks that each outcome's decided step is written when the trace store works. No row makes the decided-step write fail. Restoring the old bare `await decidedStep(...)` would leave every row green. Add table rows where the trace write fails, for example by mocking traceStep the way registry-step.test.ts does. At least: already_done still resolves with the earlier result, already_cancelled still throws the cancelled error, expired still throws the expiry error, and run still rejects without calling the tool.

This fixes the pin by changing the general `list_workflow_runs` read tool. The tool used to filter by status in the query, then take up to 50 rows. `latestRuns` now fetches the latest 50 runs and filters them in memory. Agents and chat use this tool too. When the matching runs are older than the latest 50, they now get `[]`, which reads as 'there are none' and not as 'outside the window'. Keep the in-query status filter for the general tool. If the ticket needs a 'within the latest N' view, give it its own argument (e.g. `withinLatest: true`) or return the window so an empty result says it's bounded.

Round 2 claimed this fix: on the already_done, already_cancelled and expired paths, a failed trace write must not hide the outcome that is already settled. No test makes the decided-step write fail. The new table only checks that each outcome is written once, with the trace store working. If the `.catch` in engine.ts `decide` were removed, every row would still pass, so this is not a test of the fix. Fix: make `decidedStep`/`traceStep` fail (mock it, as registry-step.test.ts does) and add rows for already_done (must still resolve), already_cancelled (must still throw the cancelled error, not the trace error) and expired (must throw expired). Add a `run` row that must fail closed, with the tool never called.

The new `pg_advisory_xact_lock` claims that overlapping exports of the same (tenant, day) can't both record it. This round adds no test that runs two real exports at once. Every test in the diff stays green if the lock line is deleted, so nothing proves the guarantee. Fix: add a race test that starts two `exportAuditDay` calls for the same tenant and day on separate connections with `Promise.all`. Assert that each key is put once, there is one recorded export, and neither call fails with ObjectLockedError. The test must fail when the lock is removed.

The round-2 fix made the confirm path's non-`run` decided steps best-effort so that a trace-store failure can't hide an outcome that is already settled. The cancel path was missed. `cancelAction` awaits `decidedStep(action, "cancelled")` after `cancelCard` has already claimed the key as cancelled. If that trace insert fails, the exception goes to `cancelChat`/`outcomeOf`, and the person sees an error for a cancel that did take effect. Fix: make the cancel's decided step best-effort and log its failure, the same as `decide()` does for confirm. Add a variant row for cancel to decided-trace-fail.test.ts.

In the write-tool shim in `runTurn`, the card goes into `pending` before `await traceStep({ kind: "pending" ... })` runs. If that step write throws, the tool call fails toward the model, but the card was already pushed and `append` still saves it. The person is shown a live confirm card while the model replies that the action failed. This is the same 'a trace failure must not change the outcome' class that the registry and confirm paths fixed. Fix: write the step before the push, so the card is dropped when the step fails. Or keep the push and make the step best-effort, but don't do both halves.

Every row that isn't revoked, including expired ones, gets the prompt 'Rotate the X token, keep its expiry'. For an expired credential, `keptExpiry` always throws, and only on confirm, after the person has typed the new secret into the masked field. So the main action on the rows that most need attention can never succeed as offered. Fix: for expired rows, use a prompt that asks for a new expiry date, or check `keptExpiry` when the card is proposed (before the confirm) so the card asks for `expiresAt` up front.

Rounds 2–3 fixed the Scheduler tickets so each pin resolves to exactly the rows its ticket counts (`withInLatest`, a status filter). The Keys tickets were left behind: 'Expiring in 30 days', 'Rotated in 90 days' and 'Credentials' all pin `list_secrets` with `{}`, which returns every credential. Fix: give `list_secrets` a filter (for example `expiringWithinDays` or status) and pin each ticket with the filter it counts.

The 'expiring soon' rule is written a second time. The hub computes `r.status === "active" && expiresAt - Date.now() <= EXPIRY_WINDOW_DAYS*DAY`, while KeyTickets and KeyTable use `expiringSoon(r, now)` from keys/format.ts. The hub version also accepts an active credential whose expiry has already passed but hasn't been swept yet, and reports a day count of zero or less. Fix: use the one `expiringSoon` helper in both places.

The hub's AI usage card builds its cost from aiStats and shows `$${s.costUsd.toFixed(2)} this month`. That folds unpriced calls in as $0. The AI usage screen and get_ai_usage use aiUsage/costLabel, which report those calls as unknown and never as $0 (048 AC-5). That makes two copies of the month's cost total, and they disagree. Fix: build the hub card from aiUsageTotals(scope tenant) and costLabel.

The 052 fix made findSchedule refuse an ambiguous title rather than write to the first match. entityId has the same flaw and was not fixed: it resolves a legal entity by case-insensitive name and takes the first row in name order. set_entity_zone then writes the zone to that entity and moves all of its schedules. Fix: when more than one entity matches the name, refuse and list the candidates (by id), as findSchedule does.

Re-tagging moved to chat, but the redirect that `releaseEditAction` did after `tagRelease` was deleted and nothing replaced it. Once the user confirms `tag_release` in chat, the page URL still names the old version, so on refresh or navigation it renders "Release not found". The e2e test hides this: it calls `page.goto('/delivery/releases/CON/v2.4.1')` by hand after the confirm. This is the stale-URL defect already logged against `releaseEditAction`, carried onto the new path. Fix: after a confirmed `tag_release`, chat should navigate to the release's new URL (for example, the tool result returns an href that chat follows). Alternatively, ReleasePage can look up a renamed tag and redirect to its current version. Add a test with no manual `goto`.

The change fixed the 046 class 'row pins resolve to a list, not to the record' for time (`get_timesheet`) and allocations (`get_allocation`). It left the same class in the delivery components it edits. Board cards pin `list_proposals` for the whole project. Environment rows (`EnvironmentsCard.tsx` `{...pin, label: "HRI Staging"}`) pin `list_environments`. Each deployment-history row in `ReleasePage.tsx` pins `get_release_history` for the whole release. R3 / AGENTS rule 2 requires a PinRef that resolves to that exact record. Fix: add single-record read tools (a proposal by key, an environment by name, a deployment by id) and point these pins at them.

Approve and Remind used to send the exact `weekId`. They now send a prompt that names the person by display name only ("Approve Nimal Silva's timesheet for 2026-W42"). The bulk button in ThisWeek.tsx:22 does the same with a comma-separated list of names. The tool then has to resolve a free-text name back to a week, which is ambiguous. The Void prompt in this same diff already embeds the record id (`(id ${d.id})`); these prompts don't. Fix: put the weekId(s) in the prompt, and resolve approve_week/remind_week by weekId, as the old actions did.

getAllocation falls back to a case-insensitive name match and silently takes the first person with that name. The tool description invites a name ('employee number or name'), so chat can pass one. An ambiguous name should fail (or list the matches), not quietly return one person's row. Also, `null` is returned both when the person doesn't exist and when the person is in `grid.hidden` (outside the viewer's HR access), so 'could not see' reads as 'not found' (B3).

Any `ownerName` in the input unconditionally sets `owner_user_id = null`, even when the name is unchanged or belongs to a known user. Free-text owner name and owner link can then disagree, and the opportunity loses its link to a person (AGENTS rule 4: every record says who did it/owns it). Fix: resolve ownerName to a user the way createOpportunity does, and clear the link only when no user matches. If the name can't be resolved, flag it instead of clearing.

This change deletes the BACKLOG item about row pins that resolve to a whole list, but only fixes it for time (`get_timesheet`) and allocations (`get_allocation`). The delivery rows this diff rewrites still pin a list. Each environment row pins `list_environments` (all of the project's environments). Each deployment-history row in ReleasePage.tsx:54 pins `get_release_history` (the whole history). Each board card in ProjectPage.tsx:39 pins `list_proposals` (every proposal in the project). AGENTS rule 2 / R3 says a pin must resolve to that exact record, so these count as missing pins. Fix: add one-record read tools, or optional filter arguments on the existing tools (environment name, deployment id, proposal key), and pass them in each row's PinRef.

This fix compares owner names in two ways that can disagree. `same` uses a trimmed, case-sensitive match against the stored owner_name. `ownerLink` (common.ts) uses a trimmed, case-insensitive match against the actor's name. If someone restates the current owner in a different case, `same` is false, so the update goes through `ownerLink`. Unless the actor is that owner, `ownerLink` returns null, which clears a valid user link and records the owner as unlinked. The test only covers an exact restatement. Fix: use one name-normalising helper for both comparisons, for example trim plus a locale-insensitive lower-case. Add case and spacing variants to the table-driven test.

The page now follows a re-tagged release to its new URL, but the fix stops at the URL. The comment says `router.replace` keeps the conversation open on the new page. That conversation still holds the old pins: the release pin and the new `deployPin`, both `{ projectKey, version: 'v2.4.0' }` (ReleasePage.tsx:16-18). On the next turn those pins resolve to a release that no longer exists. Pins saved in `chat.conversation` have the same problem. The new `get_deployment` makes it worse: it keys a deployment by its immutable uuid but still requires the mutable version. Fix: when `moved` is applied, rewrite the pins in this conversation whose args name the old version. Also make `get_deployment` resolve by `deploymentId` alone, with project and version only as a scope check.

`get_release` now treats every argument as optional and does not check that it was given enough to find a release. If `releaseId` is missing, it compares `r.projectKey === a.projectKey && r.version === a.version`, so a call with no arguments or only half of them (`{}`, `{ projectKey: 'CON' }`, `{ version: 'v2.3.0' }`) matches nothing and returns `null`, which reads as 'release not found'. Its sibling `get_release_history` takes the same arguments and throws 'say which release' instead. The same lookup is now written twice and the two copies disagree (B4). Fix: give both tools one input schema with a refine that requires either `releaseId` or both `projectKey` and `version`, or have `get_release` go through the same checked lookup that `getRelease` uses. Add these three incomplete-argument cases to the table test.

Instance fix of the round-3 get_release finding. The incomplete-ref check runs inside `isRelease`, and `isRelease` only runs as the `find` predicate on each row. If `listReleases(v)` returns no rows, `releaseWhere` never runs, so the call returns `null` ('not found') instead of the 'say which release' refusal. Whether a malformed call gets refused now depends on the data, so `get_release` and `get_release_history` still disagree. The new table test passes only because the fixtures give sahan visible releases. Fix: check the ref before the read (`releaseWhere(a)` at the top of `run`, or a zod `.refine` on `releaseRef`). Add a test case where the viewer can see no releases.

The repin is applied only to this tab's React `pins` state. The architecture says a conversation's pins are persisted in `chat.conversation`, and `confirmChat`/`repinOf` never rewrite the stored pins. Three cases keep the stale `{ projectKey, version: old }` or `{ projectKey, name: old }` args: reopening the conversation from History, another tab with the same conversation open, and any other conversation that pinned the same release or environment. Fix: apply `repinAll` to the stored pins on the server inside the confirm path, then return the updated pins to the client.

Saved pins are only rewritten after a rename inside `confirmChat`, and only in the confirming viewer's own conversations. Two variants still go stale. (1) `tag_release` or an environment rename run over MCP, by an agent or by a pipeline. MCP is the main channel, and nothing there calls `repinConversations`. (2) Other people's saved conversations that hold pins keyed on project key and version or on project key and name. All pins made before 057 are keyed that way, including the old `get_release` / `get_release_history` row pins. Those pins then read null, or read a different release once the old version tag is reused. Fix: make the read tools resolve old pins by id. For example, rewrite stored key-based pins to ids lazily when they are next read, or record the rename and look it up at read time. Then drop the repin step that only works for the actor in chat.

Release, environment and deployment pins are now keyed on ids so that a rename can't strand them. The new proposal pins (board card, and the release page's proposal list via `get_proposal`) are keyed on `key`, which can also change: the specclaw sync rekeys hand-made proposals (`ProposalRekeyed`). Nothing repins on a rekey. Fix: key proposal pins on the proposal id. Add an optional `proposalId` to `get_proposal`, so that a key given with it only narrows the result, the same rule used for releases.

`repinConversations` runs after `confirmAction` has committed the write, inside the same try. If the repin throws (a DB error or a timeout), the catch returns `outcomeOf(e)`. The card then shows an error or open state for a write that actually happened, the response carries no `moved`, and the page doesn't follow the re-tag. Fix: run the repin in its own try/catch after the write and still return `state: 'done'` with `moved`. Log the repin failure, or report it as a separate warning in the note.

The docstring at line 203 says one rule covers releases, environments and deployments: with an id, any key part that is also given only narrows the result. `getEnvironment` only narrows on `projectKey`. When `environmentId` is given, `name` is ignored, so this copy of the rule disagrees with `releaseWhere`/`isRelease`. Fix: also require `x.name === ref.name` when both are given, or derive all three readers from one shared helper.

After a confirmed rename, the client replaces its whole pin state with the conversation's saved pins (`setPins(o.pins)`). Pins are saved only when a turn is sent. Any pin added or removed in the drawer since the last turn is lost, or a removed one comes back, on every repinning confirm. Fix: send the `repin` to the client and apply repinAll to the current client pins, rather than overwriting them with the server copy.

The repin covers only one path: a rename confirmed through chat, and only the conversations of the person who confirmed it. Two variants are missed. tag_release or upsertEnvironment(rename) called directly over MCP (agents, pipelines) returns `repin` but nothing applies it. Other people's saved conversations keep projectKey/version or projectKey/name pins that now resolve to null; the test even asserts that the other user's pin stays stale. Fix: resolve by id instead. Make the rename service rewrite every matching saved pin, tenant-wide, in the same transaction as the write (chat.conversation is chat's own schema, so do it through a chat command, not from the delivery module). Or migrate old version- and name-keyed pins to releaseId/environmentId once, so no pin depends on a renamable key.

ruleItems() turns any failure to count a rule's rows into 0 with `.catch(() => 0)`. A rule that fails (missing column, bad subject cast, timeout) is dropped from the inventory. erase() only applies rules that appear in the inventory, so the request completes as 'Erased' while that table still holds the person's data. The person is never told and neither is the approver. Fix: record the item as 'could not check' and refuse to open or complete the request until every rule could be counted.

Erasure finds rows only through `subject` columns that hold the person's ids. Several new entries keep the person's name but have no subject column that names the person. presales.activity, presales.task, presales.risk and presales.suggestion have no subject at all. delivery.proposal's subject is `project_id` but the personal field is owner_name. These rows never appear in an access or erasure inventory, and the request still completes as erased. Fix: give each name-bearing table a subject column for the person (an owner_user_id or actor id), or fail the standard when `fields` hold a personal value that `subject` can't reach.

privacyOverview sums only `preview.counts` and ignores `preview.failed`. A rule whose preview fails reads as 0 in 'Due tonight' and in the lede ('Tonight's purge removes N records'). Nothing on screen says the rule couldn't be checked. Fix: return the failed rules and show them as unknown or needing attention.

'Data classes covered' is hard-coded as `${rules} of ${rules}` with progress 100% and 'Every personal-data table has a rule'. It counts the rules against themselves, so it can never show a gap. Fix: compare against the personal-data tables found (the check-module-standard scan, or a declared inventory), or drop the claim.

Chat retention is declared as `period: P90D, start: { at: [], idle: P90D }`. due() computes `updated_at < now() - idle - period`, so a conversation is purged only after 180 idle days. The label and TENANT_DEFAULTS say 'kept 90 days after its last message'. Fix: `start: { at: ['updated_at'] }` or `idle: 'P0D'`.

The privacy source list is hand-built twice: here and in scripts/seed-demo.ts (the test builds a third copy). Both copies leave out apiPlatform, so the `api.rate_limited` retention rule is invisible to the purge, legal holds, set_retention_period and the screen. packages/api/src/module.ts then enforces it with its own hard-coded `api.prune` deletes, which also delete api.inbound and api.delivery without a declared rule. Those deletes ignore legal holds and tenant overrides, which is exactly what 032 replaced workflows.prune for. Fix: derive the sources from the same manifest list as jobs and workflows, including api, and remove the hard-coded deletes in favour of retention entries.

[design] The SSRF guard on outgoing webhook URLs only checks the hostname text against a regex, and only when the webhook is subscribed. It does not resolve the hostname. It also misses whole classes of private addresses: internal DNS names (k3s `*.svc.cluster.local`, `metadata.google.internal`), wildcard DNS that points at private IPs (`127.0.0.1.nip.io`), `0.0.0.0`, IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`[::ffff:7f00:1]`), CGNAT 100.64/10, and decimal or octal IP forms. `deliver.ts` `post()` then calls `fetch` on the stored URL without checking again, so DNS rebinding also works. amax is a multi-tenant SaaS, so any tenant's Admin gets a signed blind POST into the provider's internal network. Fix: resolve the host at delivery time and reject private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and mapped ranges on the resolved address (pin the connection to that address). Keep the subscribe-time check as a first filter only.

Replay protection for GitHub and amax-signed calls rests on dedupe by `x-github-delivery` / `x-amax-delivery`. Those headers are not covered by the signature. GitHub sends no timestamp, and amax checks only the 5-minute window. A captured request replayed with a fresh delivery id passes the signature check and the dedupe. The screen still claims 'each event once'. Fix: dedupe on a hash of the signed body (as msgraph does) or include the id in the signed material.

Outgoing webhook masking guesses 002 classes from field names with its own regex list. That is a second copy of the sensitivity classification, and it disagrees with the modules' declared classes. For example, hr retention classes epf_number as `pay`, but classOf('epf_number') / classOf('epfNumber') is undefined. Pay data then goes unmasked to external receivers. Fix: mask from the emitting module's declared field classes, and fail closed on fields with no class.

When the tenant has no secret configured for a provider, the call is recorded as reason 'missing', the same as a request with no signature. The screen then reports it as an 'unsigned webhook call rejected … claiming to be from X'. 'We could not verify' reads as 'attacker'. Fix: record a separate reason (not_configured) and show it as a setup problem.

LIMITS hard-codes '120 a minute per token, 240 per person' and '600 a minute per person'. The real values come from rate-limit.ts defaults and the AMAX_RATE_* env overrides. The page notes also hard-code '5 failures' (MAX_FAILURES) and '5 minutes' (REPLAY_WINDOW_MS). Fix: render from the configured limits and constants.

The ✓auto retention check only parses lowercase `create table schema.t (` blocks that end with a line holding just `);`, plus `add column`. `CREATE TABLE`, `create table if not exists`, one-line tables and `alter table … add` without `column` are skipped silently, so the check passes. The manifest match is `includes('table: "x"')`, which a comment also satisfies. Fix: parse case-insensitively and with `if not exists`, and fail on migrations it can't parse.

[design] A REST call made with a service credential runs the tool as the person it acts for. Admin tools build their ServiceContext with `ctxFor(viewer, source)`, which carries no principal. So the audited actor is `user:<person>` with kind `user`, and the credential (`sp:<id>`) appears only in the trace. This breaks AGENTS rule 4 (the record must say it was an agent or service acting for the person). It also defeats the two-person rule's check that a privacy request is completed by a person, not an agent or service (`twoPersonRule` checks `actor.kind !== 'user'`). The privacy write tools have no chat-only guard, unlike `create_api_credential`, so the erasure can run with no confirm card at all. Fix: carry the principal into the ServiceContext (`actor: sp:<id>`, kind `service`, `onBehalfOf: user:<id>`), and make `open/complete_privacy_request` chat-only the way `chatOnly()` does for credentials.

[design] `completePrivacyRequest` builds the inventory from the merged ids (`req.subjects` plus the ids `resolveSubject` returns now). `erase()` applies the rules, and `privacy.erase_request` erases the audit and trace chains, using only the `req.subjects` stored when the request was opened. The legal-hold check also uses only the stored ids. Ids added since then (a new hr.person row, a resolver added by a newly installed module) are listed as erased but are never erased or checked against holds. Fix: write the merged ids back to `privacy.request.subjects` before calling `erase_request`, and use them for `about()` and the hold check.

[design] The proxy calls `takeRate` from its own copy of `@amax/core/rate-limit`. `configureRateLimits` runs only in `lib/server.ts` `getDb()`, inside the app's server bundle, and Next compiles the proxy as a separate entry, so module state is not shared. The page limiter therefore always uses the built-in defaults (AMAX_RATE_PAGE_* is ignored) and the no-op sink, so page 429s are never recorded in api.rate_limited and the 'Pages' row always shows 0. Fix: configure the limiter inside proxy.ts from `loadEnv()`, and give it a recorder or a shared store.

[design] `apiRetention` (api.rate_limited, P90D) is declared, but `setPrivacySources` in lib/server.ts never includes `api()`. The rule never reaches the 032 catalog, the screen or `set_retention_period`. Meanwhile `api.prune` is a second, hard-coded retention path: raw deletes of api.rate_limited, api.inbound and api.delivery that ignore tenant periods and legal holds. That is exactly what architecture.md says 032 replaced `workflows.prune` to stop. Fix: register the api retention entries (including inbound and delivery) as privacy sources and delete `api.prune`.

The CLI guard `import.meta.url !== `file://${process.argv[1]}`` compares a percent-encoded, symlink-resolved URL with a raw path. The two differ when the checkout path contains a space or other encoded character, or when it is reached through a symlink (Node realpaths the ESM main module, but argv[1] is only path.resolve'd). When they differ, `main()` never runs, nothing is printed, and the process exits 0, so the ✓auto retention and required-files check reports as passed without checking anything. Fix: compare with `pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href`, or move the parsers into a separate module that the CLI and the tests both import, so the CLI always runs `main()`.

[design] The fix for name-only tables matches `subjectName` columns by comparing the free-text name (lowercased and trimmed) with the requested person's name. A name does not identify a person. (1) Homonyms: an erasure anonymises the rows of everyone with the same name, and an access request (`buildPackage` uses the same `about()`) exports another person's records to the requester. A person hold also pauses the purge for the homonyms' rows. (2) Variants: 'Sam' vs 'Samantha', a maiden name, a missing middle name or a typo match nothing. Those rows stay out of the inventory, and the request still completes as 'Erased'. So name matching both over-reaches (data loss and disclosure) and under-reaches (rows left behind and reported as erased). Fix: give each name-bearing table an id column for the person (`owner_user_id` or an actor id) and match on that. If a name column must stay, list name-only hits as 'needs review' and keep them out of the automatic erase and the access export.

declaredFieldClasses builds one tenant-wide map keyed only by the normalised field name. It gives every field of a retention entry that entry's class, whatever module or table the field is on. Any event from any module that carries a field with the same name is then masked with that class. For example, a payroll entry with fields ['amount'] or ['name', 'base_salary'] under class 'pay' masks `amount` or `name` in finance and delivery webhooks. The earlier fix asked for masking from the emitting module's declared classes, not a global name map. Fix: key the classes by emitting module (the event-name prefix, or the manifest that emits it), and apply only that module's declared classes to its payloads.

Sharing the limiter through globalThis only works when the proxy and the app run in the same process, after the app has already called getDb(). On Vercel and Cloudflare (OpenNext), both required deploy targets, the proxy runs in a separate function or isolate. There the sink is always the no-op, so page 429s are never written to api.rate_limited and the 'Pages' row stays at 0. On k3s, 429s from before the first getDb() are also dropped. The previous finding asked for a recorder or a shared store. Fix: wire the rate-limit recorder in proxy.ts itself, or queue limited events somewhere the app drains, rather than relying on shared process memory.

Dedupe for GitHub calls is now the only replay protection, because GitHub sends no timestamp. It depends on api.inbound rows still existing. This diff moves api.inbound deletion into the 032 purge, where a tenant's own period overrides the declared P90D. An Admin who shortens api.inbound's period with set_retention_period also shortens how long a captured signed GitHub body can't be replayed. Fix: keep the dedupe key in its own store with a fixed minimum lifetime, outside the retention purge, or give api.inbound a floor (a statutory-style minimum) that tenant periods can't go below.

The chat retention fix (idle → `start.at: ['updated_at']`) was a major, but this diff ships no test with it. Nothing shows that a conversation idle for 91 days is now due and that one idle for 89 days is not. Under the old declaration, either would have been kept until day 180. Fix: add a table-driven purge test that drives purgeDue or previewPurge over conversations last updated 89, 91 and 179 days ago. It must fail against the old `idle: 'P90D'` declaration.

[design] 'Rules checked tonight' and 'Every rule could be checked' come only from `previewPurge().failed`. The purge doesn't touch subject or subjectName columns unless a hold is active, so a rule whose subject column is broken previews fine. Yet every access and erasure request now refuses to open on it (`assertChecked`). The screen says everything is fine while privacy requests are blocked. The new test encodes this gap (`purge=false` cases skip the overview assertion). Fix: have the overview also try each searchable rule's `about()` arm (for example, count with an empty match) and show those failures as unknown or blocking requests.

[design] The proxy and app now share the limiter through `globalThis`, which only works when both bundles run in the same process (the k3s and standalone image). On Vercel, the proxy runs as its own routing function, and Cloudflare/OpenNext runs it in a separate worker. There, `ensureRateLimits` sets the env limits but the sink stays the no-op, because `rateLimitRecorder` is only wired in `getDb()`. Page 429s are never recorded in api.rate_limited, and the 'Pages' row reads 0. PRODUCT.md requires the app to deploy unchanged to all three hosts. The fix covers only one host: wire a recorder inside proxy.ts itself, or record through a store the proxy can reach.

[design] The previous finding asked to mask from the declared classes and fail closed on fields with no class. The fix adds the declared map but keeps the regex as the only fallback: a payload field that no retention entry or tool `sensitive` declares, and that no pattern matches, is sent unmasked. The declared map is also keyed globally by field name, not by the emitting module's event, so the mask depends on whether any installed module happens to list that column in a retention entry. Fix: give each emitted event a declared field classification and refuse to send (or mask) fields without one.

The proxy now calls the app's getDb() to set up its own bundle. getDb() decides whether to wire things by checking a cache kept on globalThis (`cache.amaxDb`), and on k3s and the standalone image the proxy and the app share that globalThis. Every request passes through the proxy first, so the proxy's getDb() fills the shared cache and wires only the proxy bundle's copies of configureRuntime, setGrants, setPrivacySources, installAuthorizer, configureAi and the rate limits. When the app bundle later calls getDb(), the cache is already set, so it returns the Db without wiring the app bundle's own copies of those modules. An earlier lesson in this repo found that Next compiles the proxy and the app as separate bundles that don't share module state. So the fix moves the Vercel/Cloudflare problem onto k3s. Importing lib/server also pulls every module manifest, its UI screens, the AI providers and node:fs into the proxy bundle. Fix: key the 'already wired' flag per bundle (a module-scoped flag, separate from the shared Db cache), or give the proxy a small wiring entry that sets up only the rate limits and the recorder. Then test both orders: proxy first and app first.

The previous round's major (page 429s are not recorded when the proxy runs apart from the app) is backed only by a test that greps proxy.ts for the string 'getDb();' and checks it comes before 'takeRate('. The other new test calls wireRateLimits directly in the test process. Neither one drives the proxy. Neither would fail if getDb() skipped the rate wiring (for example, because the cache was already set, or because DATABASE_URL gating returns early), and neither would fail if the proxy's sink never reached api.rate_limited. Fix: add a table-driven test that loads the proxy entry in its own module graph (vi.resetModules or a separate import, so it doesn't share the app's state), sends page requests past the limit for at least three cases (proxy-only process, proxy first then app, app first then proxy), and checks that a row lands in api.rate_limited.

[design] Rows found only by name are now left out of the erase and the access package. That fixes the over-reach. But the request still moves to approved and completed, and the screen says 'Erased' or 'Package ready', while those rows stay unresolved. Nothing tracks them after completion, and no MCP or chat write tool lets a person erase or export a specific row once they've checked it. The Item doc says 'check and change in chat', but no such tool exists. Presales activity, task and risk still have no subject id column, so for those tables a subject's own rows are never erased or exported. Those requests are recorded as done when they are only partly done. Fix: keep a request with review rows in a 'needs review' state, not completed. Add a chat write tool that confirms or rejects named rows for the request, so they are then erased or exported. Or add the id columns the earlier finding asked for.

This is an instance fix for the round-3 finding. The proxy now has its own `proxyWired` flag, but `wireProxy` still fills the shared `globalThis.amaxDb` (`shared.amaxDb ??= createDb(...)`). This diff does not change the gate inside `getDb()` in apps/web/lib/server.ts; only the `wireRateLimits` line changed. Round 3 described that gate as `cache.amaxDb`. On k3s and the standalone image, the proxy and the app share one process, and the proxy runs first on every request. So the app's `getDb()` finds the cache already set and returns the Db without wiring its own bundle: `configureRuntime`, `setGrants`, `setPrivacySources`, `installAuthorizer`, `configureAi` and its rate limits are never called there. Fix: gate the app's wiring on a module-scoped flag in lib/server.ts, separate from the shared Db cache, or have `wireProxy` keep its Db in its own module scope and leave `globalThis.amaxDb` alone. The new 'proxy first, then the app' case would catch this if it ran, so confirm it runs with a database in CI and is not skipped by `hasDb`.

`wireProxy()` returns false when `AUDIT_HASH_KEY` is missing or no Db can be made, and the proxy ignores that return value. It goes on to call `takeRate` with the unconfigured default limits and no recorder. Nothing is logged and nothing fails, so 'could not wire' looks the same as 'wired'. Page 429s are then never recorded in `api.rate_limited`, and the `AMAX_RATE_*` limits are silently replaced by defaults. Fix: when `wireProxy()` returns false while `DATABASE_URL` is set, fail closed, or at least log or flag it as not wired. Do not limit with defaults and drop the counts.

`byName` is one all-or-nothing choice for every name-only row, across every rule. Round 3 asked for a way to confirm or reject specific named rows, and this does not give one. A request often has name-only rows in several tables (presales activity, task, risk), or several people with the same name in one table. 'include' erases or exports all of them, including a namesake's rows. 'exclude' keeps all of them, including the subject's own rows, and the request still completes. No read tool shows the approver the actual rows to 'check' before deciding; the inventory gives only counts. Fix: take the decision per rule, or better per row id. Only list rows the approver has seen through a read tool. Keep the request open until every review rule has a decision.

Every name-review test seeds a single table (pt.task) with a single name-only row. No case covers name-only rows spread across two rules, or a namesake's row with the same spelling next to the subject's. Those are the variants where the single `byName` switch goes wrong. Add table-driven cases with two review rules, and with two same-name rows that belong to different people.

Erasure only checks whether the person's own ids or name are under a hold. It ignores matter holds on the rows it is about to change. `place_legal_hold` says a hold pauses 'the purge and erasure' for a matter's records, and the purge honours it through `notHeld()`, but `erase()` calls `applyRule(tx, rule, about(rule, who))` with no hold filter. Fix: AND the erase condition with `notHeld(rule, held)`, use the same filter for the included name-only rows, and list held rows as kept in the inventory.

Several new retention entries list a personal column in `fields` but not in `subject` or `subjectName`. Requests and holds find rows only through those two lists. Missed: time.week.decided_by, time.entry.logged_by and presales.opportunity.lead_name. When the erased person is the approver, logger or lead, their rows are neither erased nor exported, and holds don't protect them. Fix: add each person column to `subject`, or to `subjectName` for names, and add a test that erases an approver.

`nameRows` lists at most 500 rows per rule (LIMIT). `decideNameRows` checks the decision against those listed rows only, then replaces the review item (whose n counts every row) with the included and excluded listed rows. Rows past 500 are never listed, never decided, never acted on, and drop out of the inventory without a trace, so the request completes. Fix: refuse to complete, or page through the rows, when the count is above the limit, and keep the unlisted rows as a review item.

A person hold copies `resolveSubject` ids into `legal_hold.subjects` when it is placed. Ids the person gains afterwards are not held. A fix in this diff re-resolves ids for erasure requests for exactly this reason, but holds still use the old snapshot. Fix: for kind='person', store the user id and re-resolve the person's ids in `held()` on each purge or erasure.

`countsAsPage` skips any request that carries a prefetch header or a `next-action` header. The client sets all of these headers. The proxy comment says skipping `rsc: 1` would let clients dodge the limit, but these headers allow the same bypass. A GET with `next-action` or `purpose: prefetch` still renders the page. Fix: exempt `next-action` only on POST, and count prefetches (at lower weight or in their own bucket) rather than not at all.

Erasure anonymises every field of a rule on any row whose subject matches. `allocations.allocation` lists `person_id` as a subject and `updated_by` as the field, and `time.week` lists `user_id` as a subject with `decided_by` as a field. Erasing an employee therefore wipes the attribution of the PM or approver, which breaks the rule that every record says who did it. It also leaves the employee's own reference (`person_id`) in place. Fix: limit each rule's fields to the subject columns that matched, or split the rules per person column.

`failure()` maps only CallerError, RateLimitedError, ToolError, Forbidden/Scope, ValidationError and errors with code not_found or invalid_input. PrivacyError and other domain refusals have no code, so they return 500 'internal' and are logged as server faults. Fix: map errors with `retryable === false` to 400 or 409 with their message.

The access package caps each section, and the audit list, at 5000 rows with `limit 5000`. Nothing records that a section was cut short, so the package presents itself as the person's complete data. Fix: count the rows first, then either page through them or mark the section as truncated and refuse to complete the request.

This round fixed the 'no secret set up' case for incoming webhooks (`not_configured` is a setup problem, not an attacker) but not for outgoing ones. If the tenant has no `amax-webhook` signing secret, `useSecret` throws on every attempt. The delivery is retried, recorded as a receiver failure and added to `failures`. After `MAX_FAILURES` events the webhook is switched off, and the screen tells the admin to fix the receiver. `subscribeWebhook` does not check that the secret exists either. Fix: refuse to subscribe when the signing secret is missing, and treat `SecretNotConfiguredError` at delivery as a non-retryable setup error that does not count toward switch-off.

GitHub and Microsoft Graph calls carry no signed timestamp, so the `api.inbound` dedupe row is their only replay protection, as the comment here says. The purge still deletes those rows after the P90D `minimum`. After that, a captured signed GitHub delivery or Graph notification verifies again and is accepted as new. The dedupe key is a body hash, not personal data. Fix: keep the dedupe hashes of verified rows with no time-based delete (for example, a separate non-personal table), or tie GitHub and Graph acceptance to a freshness field inside the signed body.

Rate-limited counts are held in memory and written only by a `setTimeout` five seconds later. On Vercel and Cloudflare, where the proxy runs in its own function or worker, the instance is often frozen or recycled before the timer fires. Those 429s are never written to `api.rate_limited`, and the screen shows 'None this week'. Requests that were limited read as no limiting. Fix: write the count in the request path (a `waitUntil`/`after()` hook on the proxy or route) or flush synchronously when a 429 is answered.

When AMAX_BASE_URL is unset, `siteUrl()` quietly uses `http://localhost:3000`, even in production. This is also a second copy of the public-origin logic in `apps/web/lib/server.ts:112` `baseUrl()`, and that copy throws in production when the URL is missing (B4). The two can disagree: `server.ts:37` only requires AMAX_BASE_URL once DATABASE_URL is set, but AC-2 says the marketing page must render without a database. So a DB-less production deploy publishes localhost URLs and nothing flags it. Fix: build `siteUrl()` on the same rule as `baseUrl()` (fail in production when unset, and allow only loopback outside it), keep that rule in one place, and add a variant test (prod unset, prod set, dev unset).

AC-3 requires every claim to match a shipped module and every unbuilt area to be marked "Coming". Only "People and payroll" is marked Coming, and that one is half wrong: hr and leave are shipped, payroll is not. These are presented as available but have no module: Finance and sales (contracts, billing milestones, expenses, Xero/QuickBooks/Business Central integration), Operations (IT assets and access, incidents, insights) and Delivery forecasts. The shipped modules are only allocations, compliance, delivery, hr, keyflow, learning, leave, notifications, presales and time. `tests/e2e/marketing.spec.ts:16` (`Coming` count = 1) locks in the wrong state. Fix: mark each unbuilt capability or area as Coming, or drop it, and have the test check the Coming set against `modules/*/module.ts`.

knownOrigin() uses a bare catch {} that turns every error from baseUrl() into null. That includes loadEnv()'s "invalid environment configuration" error, for example a malformed AMAX_BASE_URL that fails z.url(). So "origin not configured" and "config could not be read" give the same result, and both are silent. The page then drops its canonical and OG URLs, robots drops its sitemap line, and sitemap.xml returns 200 with an empty list. AC-7 fails in production, and nothing logs or flags it. This is the case the previous finding raised ("nothing flags it"): the localhost URL is gone, but the silence is not. Fix: catch only the expected "AMAX_BASE_URL unset" case. Let invalid configuration throw, or at minimum surface it, for example by logging a fixed message once in production. Add variants to site-origin.test.ts: production with a malformed AMAX_BASE_URL, and production with it unset (does it flag?).

Step 2 tells the public that "Each write waits for a confirm". Step 1 says agents write through MCP. Only chat's pending-action confirm holds a write until someone approves it. A write tool called over /api/mcp runs straight away. The module standard says a `service: null` write "still works over MCP but never becomes a chat card", and packages/mcp/src/registry.ts has no confirm step. So the page tells prospects that agent writes are gated when they are not, which breaks AC-3 ("Every claim matches PRODUCT.md or shipped modules"). The prose check in marketing-areas.test.ts only looks for Coming words in HERO_LEDE, DESCRIPTION and the live claims, so it cannot catch a wrong claim about how the product behaves. Fix: reword the step so the confirm applies to chat only, for example "In chat, amax asks before it changes anything. Every write, from chat, MCP or the UI, is permission-checked, audited and attributed". Make the same change to the mock's step 2.

No test proves this fix. The only test change adds STEPS to the `prose` table, and that test only checks that no Coming-feature word appears. The old step 2 ("Each write waits for a confirm…") has no Coming words, so the test passes with or without the fix. Nothing guards against a step claiming that every write, or MCP writes, waits for a confirm. Fix: add a table-driven assertion over every copy surface (STEPS, HERO_LEDE, DESCRIPTION, the live claims, and ideally the mock's 062 section). It should reject an unqualified confirm claim (e.g. /each write waits for a confirm/i, /every write waits/i, /asks before it changes anything/ unless the same sentence scopes it to chat) and require the confirm sentence to say "In chat". Check that it fails on the pre-fix STEPS.

The page says commits log time, but they don't. `HERO_LEDE` says "Commits close tasks and log time", `DESCRIPTION` says "Agents log time", and the captions (`amax-product.en.vtt` 00:09–00:15: "And logs the time for the person it acted for. Wednesday goes from 5.0 to 7.5 hours") show hours landing on the timesheet with nobody acting. What ships is different. `modules/time/suggestions.ts` `commitTimeHandler` turns a commit's hours into a `time.commit-draft` suggestion, and only the person's acceptance logs a draft entry ("Only the person accepting it logs the entry"). The architecture's agent rule (006) says the same: an agent's output is a suggestion. The page therefore claims an automatic write that the product refuses to make, which also contradicts its own "Agents record, people decide" framing. Fix: say commits suggest time that the person accepts (for example "Commits close tasks and draft your time"), make the video caption show the accept step, and add the hero, description and VTT text to a test that rejects 'log(s) time' unless it is tied to accepting.

The new guard against claiming that time gets logged misses the pre-fix wording and lets through sentences that make the claim. `TIME` only matches the words `time` or `hours`. Its `[^.]*` stops at the decimal point in amounts like "2.5", so "logs 2.5 h" and "logs 2.5 hours" never match. The old caption "Wednesday goes from 5.0 to 7.5 hours" has no 'log' word at all, so it doesn't match either. `accepted()` passes any sentence that contains 'draft' or 'suggest' anywhere, even when that word isn't about the time. So the test covers only the hero wording the reviewer named, not the whole class. Fix: make the claim check about the hours themselves, for example `(log|add|book|record|fill)\w*` near a number followed by `h` or `hours`, or `timesheet`, and use a sentence split that doesn't break on decimals. Require the accept or draft word to be in the same clause as the hours. Add the old mock caption and the old VTT cue as rejected cases.

This is still a partial fix, not a fix for the whole class. WRITES is a hand-written list of verb forms, and it leaves out the -ing forms and other common ways of saying hours get written. `\b(log|logs|logged|...)\b` does not match 'logging', 'adding', 'booking', 'recording', 'filling' or 'tracking'. Verbs like 'enter', 'enters', 'entered', 'writes', 'updates' and 'puts' aren't in the list at all. A sentence using any of them can claim hours are written with no accept step, and the guard passes it. Fix: match verb stems (`log\w*|add\w*|book\w*|record\w*|fill\w*|track\w*|enter\w*|writ\w*|updat\w*|lands?|goes from`). Add an -ing case and an 'enter' case to the rejected table.

This is still a partial fix. The verbs the reviewer named now match as stems, but the three alternatives at the end of the same regex are still fixed word forms: `lands?`, `goes from` and `do(?:es)? that`. Their other forms ('landed', 'landing', 'went from', 'going from', 'did that', 'doing that') are the same class of miss the previous finding was about. The list also still leaves out common verbs for writing hours, such as 'submit', 'post', 'save' and 'create'. Any of these can claim that hours are written with no accept step, and the guard passes it. Fix: turn the remaining alternatives into stems (`land\w*|(?:go(?:es|ing)?|went) from|(?:do(?:es|ing)?|did) that`) and add `submit\w*|post\w*|sav\w*|creat\w*`. Then add 'landed', 'went from' and 'submits' cases to the rejected table.

The comment says the guard is now a closed list, but only the verb side is closed. The guard first decides whether a clause is about hours, using the HOURS regex, and HOURS is still a hand-written list of noun forms. It matches `hours` (plural only), `<n> h`, `<n> hour(s)`, `time…` and `bookkeeping`. It misses the singular `hour` with no number before it, `hrs`/`hr`, `half an hour` and words like `worklog` or `effort`. A clause using any of those never reaches the OWNED check, so it passes whatever verb it uses. This is the same class of miss as the last three rounds, moved from the verb list to the noun list. Fix: widen HOURS to stems such as `\bhours?\b|\bhrs?\b|\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:h|hrs?|hours?)\b|\btime\w*|\bbookkeeping\b|\bworklog\w*`. Then add 'Each commit logs an hour for Kasun.', 'Agents log 7.5 hrs.' and 'The agent books half an hour.' to the rejected table. That table has no case for these forms today.

OWNED only checks that a clause contains one of the words accept, draft or suggest. It does not check that those words describe the hours. A clause that names them in a negation, or about something else, still passes. The guard is meant to catch any clause that says hours get written with no draft or accept step, and this lets that exact claim through. Fix: treat OWNED as satisfied only when no negation (`no|without|never|skip\w*|before`) comes before it in the clause. Or flip the check so the clause must say the hours are what gets drafted, suggested or accepted. Add 'Agents log 2.5 h without a draft.' and 'Commits log hours with no accept step.' to the rejected table.

[design] The 'commits log time' claim was a major in earlier rounds. Time from a commit is only a `time.commit-draft` suggestion until the person accepts it. The hero, description, Problem card, captions and mock were fixed to say agents 'draft' the time. In the final diff no test guards that fix any more. The earlier `TIME` check is gone from marketing-confirm.test.ts, and nothing in apps/web/tests matches log/logs time, timesheet or bookkeeping wording. marketing-areas.test.ts only looks for the words of Coming features, and marketing-confirm only checks confirm claims. Fix: bring back a table-driven check over `surfaces()`. Any sentence about time or hours (log, logs, logged, record, track, fill in the timesheet, bookkeeping) must also say it is drafted or suggested and that the person accepts it. Add a rejects table with at least 'Commits close tasks and log time.', 'Agents log time.' and 'In amax, agents fill in the timesheet over MCP.'

This diff grants `delivery:proposal:sync@assigned` to Engineer and `@managed` to PM so they can use sync_specclaw. The same permission also opens the existing `sync_proposal` MCP tool (mcp.ts:76). That tool calls syncProposal directly and skips every 062 guard: it accepts `phase: "released"`, it can move a proposal back a phase, it never checks the linked repo or staleness, and it can rekey hand-made proposals. Before this change only Admin and service principals held this permission. Fix: give the push its own permission (e.g. `delivery:proposal:push`) and grant that one instead. Or put the 062 guards (no Released, no step back) inside syncProposal so that every caller gets them.

The retention entry for delivery.sync_push uses `action: "anonymise"`, and core/privacy/apply.ts runs that rule as an UPDATE. amax_app gets only `select, insert, delete` on the table. Erasure, and later the daily purge, then fail with 'permission denied', so a person who pushed can't be erased (032, a legal duty). Fix: add `update` to the grant, as delivery.task and delivery.commit_time have.

`repoUrl` is the raw output of `git remote get-url origin`. For HTTPS remotes this often holds a credential (`https://x-access-token:ghp_…@github.com/…`). The plugin sends it to amax, and the MCP server writes every call's args into the append-only `core.trace_event` (packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41), so the token is stored for good. normaliseRepo strips the userinfo only after the trace is written. Fix: strip the userinfo in the reader before sending, e.g. send `normaliseRepo(url)`, and regenerate the bundle.

The stale check trusts the client's `committedAt` and sets no upper bound on it. Once a push with a future date is applied, every later real push on that branch reads as stale until that date passes. The commit date can come from a skewed machine clock or a hand-written payload. Fix: refuse a `committedAt` later than now() plus a small skew, and/or order the stale check by server-side `at`.

The read in lastApplied, the apply and the recordPush each run in their own transaction, with no lock on the project and branch. Two pushes running at once can both pass the stale check, and the older commit can then land after the newer one. The guarantee 'never from a commit older than the last one applied' has no two-session test. Fix: take a lock per project and ref (an advisory lock, or `select … for update` on the project) around the check and the apply. Add a test that runs two real sessions.

pushRefusal only stops a phase from moving back. The stale check is per branch, so a lagging branch can still overwrite main's newer title, meta (pr, verdict) and tasks_done with older values. That contradicts the comment 'A branch that lags main must not undo what main already moved forward'. Fix: run the staleness check across all branches of the project, or refuse field regressions for each record (tasksDone dropping, pr or verdict being cleared).

With dryRun false, each record is a separate syncProposal write, and recordPush runs only after all of them succeed. If a record throws anything other than KeyTakenError, the earlier records stay written but no sync_push row is recorded. The Repo sync card then shows nothing, and lastApplied doesn't know about this commit, so the stale guard misses it. Fix: record the push as failed or partial, with its counts, in a finally/catch, or apply everything inside one transaction.

An applied push with only `skipped` entries still writes a sync_push row and an audit event. Archived changes that aren't yet Released always come back as skipped ('released comes from Prod deployments'), so the same unchanged state writes a new row and audit on every push. That contradicts the README's 'A push with nothing new writes nothing'. The AC-7 test passes only because its fixture leaves out the archived change. Fix: write the row only when created or updated is non-zero, or only when the skipped set differs from the last applied one.

`lastApplied` and the card's "Last sync" line are worked out only from the 20 most recent rows. Refused pushes write a row on every run, so they can push the last applied push out of that window. The card then reports that nothing was ever applied. Fix: query the latest applied push separately (as `lastApplied()` already does for the stale gate), and don't infer it from a truncated list.

Instance fix (B1). The credential is now removed only inside the amax plugin. The server still accepts a repo URL that contains a username or token, and the MCP server writes every call's raw args to the append-only core.trace_event before the tool runs (packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41). Two paths still store a token permanently: (1) `link_project_repo` (mcp.ts:90, chat intent chat.ts:11), where a PM types or pastes the repo URL; (2) any other MCP client calling `sync_specclaw`. There is also a second copy of the stripping logic: `withoutCredentials` in the plugin and `normaliseRepo` on the server (B4). Fix: redact the userinfo part of URL-shaped args before the trace step writes them, or reject any repoUrl that contains userinfo in both tools' input schemas. Also add a test that calls the tool and then checks the trace row.

This only partly fixes last round's lagging-branch finding. Comparing commit times does not tell you whether a branch includes main's changes. Say a branch was cut from an older main, and a later commit on it touches only another change. Its commit time is newer, so every other proposal in the push passes the stale check. Its older title, tasksTotal, lane, acs and the rest of meta then overwrite what main had already synced. Only phase, pr and verdict are protected. The new SKILL.md step 4 makes this worse: `--apply` now applies unattended whenever the other skips are 'would move back' or 'stale', so the field regressions are applied with no review. Fix: refuse a push from a non-default ref for proposals it didn't change against its merge-base, or refuse field regressions per record (title, tasksTotal and meta that differ from the stored values while the phase is behind). Add a test with a forked branch that has a newer commit time.

The per-proposal stale mark (`meta.committedAt`) does not move forward reliably, so an older commit can still be applied. (a) When a newer push leaves a proposal unchanged, the row is skipped (`unchanged` → continue), so committedAt stays at the older time. (b) Every other writer replaces meta wholesale without committedAt: the self-sync (`syncSpecclaw` / bin.ts) and the `sync_proposal` tool. That removes the mark, and the next push from any older commit passes. Fix: keep the mark in its own column, or a per-project or per-proposal table, that every sync writes. Advance it even when the content is unchanged. Give the stale gate one source of truth.

The project row lock protects the per-proposal checks but not the repo check. pushSpecclaw reads `repo_url` in its own transaction without a lock and compares it there. applyPush later takes `for update` on the project but never checks repo_url again. A relink that commits between the check and the apply lets a push from the repo that was just unlinked go through. Fix: compare repo_url inside applyPush, using the row it locks (`project.repo_url`), and refuse there.

The concurrency test (`Promise.all([push(at(13)), push(at(14))])`) does not force the two pushes to overlap. If the 14:00 push finishes before the 13:00 push starts, the stale check refuses the 13:00 one and the test passes. If the 13:00 push runs first, the test also passes. Only a real overlap shows whether the lock in applyPush matters. Separately, upsertSpecProposal takes the same row lock on its first write, so deleting applyPush's early lock still leaves the test green most of the time. Fix: hold the first push's transaction open after it reads stored rows (a barrier, or a session holding the lock), start the second, and assert that it blocks. Then the test fails when the early `for update` is removed.

When dryRun is false and nothing is created or updated, the push returns `outcome: "applied"` and writes no sync_push row, even when every record was skipped as stale, as a step back, or as a held key. 'Nothing applied' and 'nothing new' now give the same answer. The README says 'Each applied or refused push is a delivery.sync_push row', yet a push refused record by record leaves no trace on the Repo sync card. Fix: return a distinct outcome (e.g. `skipped`/`nothing new`) and record a row when the skipped set contains anything other than the standing expected skips, or when it differs from the last recorded push.

The test for the round-1 erasure blocker only checks `has_table_privilege` and runs an `update … where false`. It never drives the real erasure or purge path (core/privacy apply with the delivery.sync_push `anonymise` rule). It would stay green if the rule's fields, its subject columns or apply.ts's UPDATE didn't match the grant. Fix: open and complete an erasure for a person who pushed (or run purgeDue past P7Y), and assert that actor_id and for_user_id are nulled on their sync_push rows, for the actor-only, for_user-only and both-columns variants.

This only fixes one case of the credential leak (B1). `RepoUrl` rejects a URL that contains a user or token, but `packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41` writes the raw `args` to the append-only `core.trace_event` before `registry.call` validates them. The refusal therefore comes after the token is already stored for good. The refine also catches only the `scheme://user@` form. A token in scp form (`x-access-token:ghp_x@github.com:org/repo`) passes the refine, and `normaliseRepo` then strips it, so the call succeeds and the token stays in the trace. The new test checks only the service's error message. It never calls the tool over MCP and never looks at the trace row. Fix: redact the userinfo in URL-shaped args (or in all string args) inside `traceStep`/the MCP handler before the trace write. Also refuse any `user:secret@` prefix in every form. Add a tool-level test that calls the tool and then asserts the trace row holds no token.

The 'default branch covers everything' gate trusts a `defaultRef` that the client sends, and the schema falls back to "main" when it is missing. Any MCP caller, or a hand-edited payload, can set `defaultRef` equal to its own lagging branch. That branch then counts as default and overwrites every change with its older title, tasks and meta, which is the regression last round's finding described. Fix: keep the default branch on the project (set when the repo is linked, or read once from the forge) and compare `ref` against that stored value. Don't let the payload decide which ref is trusted. Add a test where a branch push claims `defaultRef` = its own ref.

Records dropped by the branch filter (`p.records.filter(x => onDefault || x.dir === own)`) leave no trace. They are not counted, not listed in `skipped`, and don't set `needsReview`. With the plugin's `defaultRefOf` falling back to "main" whenever `origin/HEAD` isn't set (plugins/amax/scripts/src/read-specclaw.ts:25), this hits real cases: a repo whose default is `master`, a detached-HEAD CI checkout (`ref` = "HEAD"), or a clone with no origin/HEAD. Every record is filtered, and the push returns `outcome: "unchanged"` with zero counts and `needsReview: false`, so `--apply` treats it as fine and nothing ever syncs. The same failure makes the plugin's fallback a fail-open default (B6). Fix: report each filtered record as a skip (e.g. `FLT-101: not this branch's change`). When the ref matches no record at all, return a distinct outcome or set `needsReview`. Have the plugin fail, or send an explicit unknown, instead of guessing "main".

The new `attempt(ctx, plan, quiet)` path commits writes to `delivery.proposal` (the `synced_commit_at` UPDATE in applyPush) inside a bare `getRuntime().db.transaction`, outside `defineService()`. That write gets no audit row, no service permission check and no events. AGENTS.md core rule 5 says writes go through `defineService()`, and the architecture lists the only three exemptions, which don't include this one. Before this round the bare transaction was always rolled back, so it never mattered. Fix: advance the marks inside a defineService (for example a `delivery.sync.mark` service, audited by count), or always go through `applied` and record the quiet case there.

The lock test stays green with applyPush's early `for update` removed. Without that lock, the first `attempt` still blocks: the other session holds the FLT-102 row lock (from its UPDATE), and `upsertSpecProposal` also locks the project. So `waited` is still true. After the release, that first attempt counts `updated: 1` and is rolled back (keep=false). `applied()` then runs in a fresh transaction, reads the committed 15:00 mark and skips the record as stale. Both assertions pass. The test also plants the competing state with hand-written SQL instead of a second real push. Fix: have the other session hold only the project row lock (no write to FLT-102), and assert that the push is still blocked before upsertSpecProposal runs. Or run two real `pushSpecclaw` calls with a barrier, and check that the result changes when the early lock is removed.

`STANDING` treats every 'would move back' and 'stale' skip as expected, even when it comes from the default branch. The README and SKILL justify those skips with 'a branch behind main', which doesn't apply to a main push. A main push that would step a phase back points to a real problem, such as a reverted or rewritten state.json. Today it is silent: outcome 'unchanged', no sync_push row, needsReview false, and --apply goes ahead unattended. The classification also works by regex-matching the message strings built in `refusal()`, a second copy of those strings (B4), so rewording a message flips needsReview. Fix: return structured skip reasons ({key, code}) from refusal(), and count move-back and stale as standing only when `!onDefault`.

Instance fix of the stale-mark finding. Only sync_specclaw advances `proposal.synced_commit_at`. The other writers of the same specclaw rows, the self-sync (`syncSpecclaw` / bin.ts via syncProposal's service) and the `sync_proposal` tool, never set it. The stale gate still has no single source of truth: after a self-sync from a newer main commit, the column still holds the older push time, so an older commit passes the gate and overwrites what the self-sync wrote. Fix: have upsertSpecProposal set `synced_commit_at = greatest(...)` for every writer that knows its commit time, or refuse pushes for rows whose last writer recorded no mark. Add a test that self-syncs and then pushes an older commit.

This only fixes one case of last round's stale-mark finding. upsertSpecProposal moves `synced_commit_at` only when the caller passes `committedAt`, and that input is optional on `sync_proposal` (mcp.ts:79). The round-3 finding named the `sync_proposal` tool as a writer, but its existing callers, the 008 CI credentials and specclaw, still send no commit time. Their writes therefore change title, phase and tasks without moving the mark. The README now says the mark is 'set by every writer that knows its commit time', but nothing makes a writer give that time. The new test covers only the syncSpecclaw/bin path, which is the one variant that passes it. Fix: make `committedAt` required for `source: "specclaw"` writes through sync_proposal, or have the push refuse (flag `needsReview`) any proposal whose last specclaw write recorded no mark. Add `sync_proposal` without `committedAt` as a row in the AC-8 variant table, beside the self-sync row.

This round fixed the bare-transaction blocker by deleting the mark update for unchanged records, so the stale-mark fix now regresses. The mark moves only inside upsertSpecProposal, which runs only for rows that change. A push or a 039 self-sync whose record already matches the stored row leaves `synced_commit_at` at the older commit. A later push from a commit between the two then passes the stale gate. The same gap is in sync/import.ts, which calls syncProposal only for changed rows. The test hides this: its expected mark was changed from 10:00 to 09:00. Fix: inside the audited service transaction (`applied`, or a small defineService mark step), advance the mark for every record the push covered, unchanged ones included, and do the same for the self-sync. Add a variant test: an unchanged push from a newer commit, then an older commit with different content, which must be skipped as stale.

The self-sync moves the mark for changed rows and unchanged rows, but its third write path doesn't move it. The withdraw loop (lines 78-81) calls `syncProposal` without `committedAt`, so a proposal the self-sync withdraws keeps its old mark. This also isn't fail-closed: `committedAt` is still optional on `syncSpecclaw` (line 44) and on the `syncProposal` service input (services.ts:207), and when it's missing every mark update is silently skipped. Only the MCP tool's schema was tightened, so the service and importer still let a specclaw write leave no mark. Fix: pass `opts.committedAt` on the withdraw write, and make `committedAt` required on `syncSpecclaw`. Also require it in `SyncInput` whenever `source` is 'specclaw', or refuse such writes without it. Add a withdraw-then-older-push row to the AC-8 variant test.

When a repo is relinked without `defaultBranch`, the stored `repo_default_ref` is kept even if the relink points to a different repo. The new repo then gets the old repo's default branch, which decides which pushes may update every change. Fix: keep the stored branch only when `normaliseRepo(input.repoUrl)` equals the stored `repo_url`. Otherwise require `defaultBranch`, the same way a first link does. Add the repo-change relink as a test row.

This round makes `committedAt` required on `SyncInput` and on `markSynced` (line 243), and now every `sync_proposal` and self-sync write moves the stale mark with it. Neither schema has the future-date bound that `PushInput` has (push.ts:36, `SKEW_MS`). The `sync_proposal` MCP tool schema (mcp.ts:79) doesn't have it either. The rule "a commit time from a skewed clock must not make every later push stale" therefore exists only in push.ts. `markSyncedRows` uses `greatest()`, so a future mark can never be lowered. Fix: define the bounded `committedAt` schema once, export it, and use it in `PushInput`, `SyncInput`, `markSynced` and the `sync_proposal` tool. Add a variant test for a future `committedAt` on each path: push, `sync_proposal` and self-sync.

The withdraw fix only covers the run that first withdraws a proposal. On every later self-sync, line 77 skips rows that already have `meta.withdrawn` set. Those rows are left out of `same` and get no `syncProposal`, so their stale mark stays at the commit that first withdrew them. That is the same unchanged-row hole that round 4 fixed for present proposals, now in the withdrawn variant: main at a newer commit still says the change is gone, but the mark doesn't move. `applyPush` then accepts any default-branch push dated after the first withdrawal, and `desired()` builds `meta` without `withdrawn`, so the push brings the proposal back. Fix: put already-withdrawn keys that are still missing into the `markSynced` key list (`same`), so the mark moves for every proposal the self-sync read, absent ones included. Add a table row to the AC-8 test: withdraw at T1, self-sync again at T3 with the folder still gone, then a default-branch push at T2 (T1 < T2 < T3) must be skipped as stale.

This fix adds `tabIndex={-1}` so that `play()` can focus the video. But after `started` flips, the Play button is gone and the native controls are the only way to work the video. A shadow host with a negative tabindex takes itself and its shadow-tree controls out of the Tab order. Once keyboard focus leaves the video, Tab can't reach it again, so the video can't be paused, sought or have its captions toggled. This breaks AGENTS.md core rule 8 (keyboard-complete, WCAG 2.2 AA 2.1.1). Fix: remove `tabIndex={-1}`, since a `<video controls>` is already focusable, or set it to `tabIndex={0}`. Extend the AC3 e2e so that it Tabs away from the video, Shift+Tabs back, and asserts the video or its controls get focus again.

This test does not prove the fix it was written for. The test only runs in Chromium (playwright.config.ts:12). In Chromium, a `<video controls>` with tabIndex 0 sends Tab from the host into the controls in its own shadow tree. Shift+Tab then goes back to the host. So `toBeFocused()` (activeElement is retargeted to the host) passes even though focus never left the video. The previous finding was about reaching the video again after focus has moved somewhere else on the page, and that path is still untested. It is also one case, not a table of variants. Fix: write a table-driven test. (a) Focus something after the tour, such as the first link in the next section, and Shift+Tab until activeElement is the video or one of its controls. (b) Focus the skip link or something before the tour and Tab forward until the video is reached. (c) Assert that a keyboard-only key, such as Space on the focused video or its controls, toggles `paused`. Check that each case fails with `tabIndex={-1}`.

This only partly fixes the test (B1 applied to the test). The loop now reaches the video from outside it, once from before and once from after, which covers variants (a) and (b) of the round-2 finding. Variant (c) is still missing: nothing checks that the video can be operated from the keyboard once it has focus. The original defect was that keyboard users lost the native controls. `toBeFocused()` is retargeted to the host, so it only proves the host or its shadow tree has focus. It does not prove a key press reaches the controls. That leaves two cases, both about focus, and none about operation. Fix: add a third row. Focus the video by keyboard (Tab from the last queue button), press Space (or `k`/Enter on the focused control), and assert that `paused` flips. Press it again and assert it flips back. Check that this row fails when `tabIndex={-1}` is set or `controls` is removed.

This fixes the named case only. The round-3 finding asked for a round trip: press Space and assert `paused` flips, then press it again and assert it flips back. The new row checks only the first half, playing → paused. It also never checks the state right before the key press. It does not assert `paused === false` or `toBeFocused()` after the Tab on line 23. So `paused === true` only shows that playback stopped. It does not show that the key press operated the control. Fix: (1) After the Tab on line 23, assert `toBeFocused()` and `paused === false`. (2) Press Space and assert `paused === true`. (3) Press Space again and assert `paused` returns to `false` (or `currentTime` advances). Put these steps in the keyboard table so the operation check sits with the two focus rows.

Step 3 says "In chat or on the screen, a person accepts, approves or promotes." The product doesn't work that way. AGENTS.md rule 1 and R3 say every write goes through chat's pending-action confirm, and screens only offer an IntentButton that opens chat. The app's own suggestions page says "Decisions happen in chat." (apps/web/app/(app)/suggestions/page.tsx:35). AC-6 requires that "confirms are scoped to chat". This is the same overclaim as 062's "Each write waits for a confirm" finding. Fix: say decisions are made in chat, for example "In chat, a person accepts, approves or promotes; the screen pins the record and opens chat." Apply the same fix to the 064 mock step.

The FAQ says data lives "In the region you pin for each legal entity". The product has one data region per tenant, not one per legal entity: snapshots, exports and buckets are keyed on "the tenant's data region" (docs/operations.md:9, 63-65), and nothing in packages/ ties a region to an entity. AC-6 requires claims to match the product. Fix: say "In the data region you choose for your workspace", and keep the retention and legal-hold part. Make the same change in the mock FAQ.

The play button doesn't meet AC-3. AC-3 requires a target of 64 px or more labelled "Play the 35-second product tour". The CSS makes it 56 px tall (`.m2 .play{height:56px}`) and 48 px at ≤480 px, and its accessible name is "Play the tour · 35 s, captions". The e2e test matches it with /Play the tour/, so it never checks the required label or size. Fix: set the height to at least 64 px at every breakpoint, use the AC's label (or change the AC on purpose), and assert both in marketing-video.spec.ts.

The CSS fix covers every breakpoint, but the test does not. The round-7 finding pointed out that the ≤480 px rule shrank the button to 48 px. This test checks the 64 px target only at Playwright's default 1280×720 viewport, because playwright.config.ts sets no viewport or projects. So the breakpoint where the defect actually was is never checked. Fix: make the size check table-driven over viewports such as 1440, 768 and 390 px. At each one, call page.setViewportSize, then assert that the button found by the exact name 'Play the 35-second product tour' is at least 64 px tall.

The FAQ says data lives in your region "with retention rules and legal holds per record type". Retention is set per record type, but legal holds are not. A hold names a person or a matter (`privacy.legal_hold`, `packages/core/src/privacy/holds.ts`, `complete.ts:25`). Any rule with no `subject` column pauses entirely while any hold is active (docs/architecture.md, Retention and erasure). So the page tells buyers about a hold model the product doesn't have. The same sentence is in the 064 mock section (.specclaw/mock/index.html:2401). Fix both copies, for example: "with retention rules per record type and legal holds per person or matter".

Three of the new hero queue cards make claims the product doesn't back up (AC-6: the claims still match the product). (1) hr1's outcome says 'Approved by you · calendar and allocations updated', but approving leave doesn't change allocations: modules/allocations/server/forecast.ts hard-codes leaveAdjusted: false, and the allocations screen says 'Booked leave isn't subtracted'. (2) hr2 is credited to 'Onboarding agent, for HR', but modules/onboarding has no agent or suggestion kind. It is also credited to a team, which breaks rule 4: an agent acts for a person. (3) pm3 offers 'Move 20% to December' from 'Allocations agent', but the agent's suggestion trims the person's largest project (modules/allocations/suggestions.ts:46); it doesn't move time to another month.
