Fix: rewrite these cards so they match shipped behaviour, or swap in cards for flows that ship. Then check every QUEUES entry, not only these three. The prose tests only scan for confirm wording, Coming items and time claims, so none of these are caught.

Each queue action removes its own button ({!done[c.id] && <button…>}) and doesn't move focus anywhere. A keyboard user loses focus to <body>, and the next Tab starts over at the skip link. This breaks AC-2 ('every action is keyboard-operable with visible focus') and rule 8 (keyboard-complete). Fix: after resolving a card, focus a stable target (the card's outcome line with tabIndex=-1, the next card's action, or the tab list). Add an e2e step: press Enter on an action, then check document.activeElement is inside the queue and that Tab moves on to the next control.

This fixes the named defect for hr2 (the card no longer credits a team or a nonexistent onboarding agent), but the rewritten card still describes a flow the product doesn't have. That breaks the round-1 finding's 'check every QUEUES entry' (AC-6). The card says HR presses 'Start onboarding' for a new hire. But modules/onboarding/README.md:3 and :8 say checklists are 'started by hr's events': handler `onboarding.joiner` runs on `hr.person.joined`. `start_checklist` exists only 'for people recorded before onboarding was installed' (README:13). So a fresh recruitment hire never waits on HR to start onboarding. The real human decision in that hand-off is recruitment's 'Add to HR' (the hiring agent's `recruitment.hired` suggestion, recruitment README:6/:14). Fix: make hr2 that decision, e.g. 'Mateo Rossi accepted the offer' with action 'Add to HR' and outcome 'Added by you · onboarding checklist started · in chat', credited to the hiring agent acting for a named person. Or swap in another shipped HR decision.

This fixes the named defect: hr2 no longer describes the 'Start onboarding' flow, which the product doesn't have, and certification reminders are a shipped feature (learning's remind_certification and the Remind chip). But the rewritten card makes a new claim the product doesn't back, which breaks AC-6 ('claims still match the product'). The card says 'Certification recorded by Liam Walsh'. Recording a certification needs `learning:certification:record`, and modules/learning/module.ts:23 grants that to HR only (README:13). This same queue presents Liam Walsh as an Engineer (en1 'Accepted by you, Liam Walsh'), so he can't record his own certificate. Fix: credit the recording to an HR person (e.g. 'Recorded in learning by <HR name>'). Before marking AC-6 met, check that the card's other fields (holder, actor, action) can each be done by the role the card names.

`holds()` writes its own copy of the grant matcher from packages/auth/src/can.ts:26-29 and :56-58. The two can disagree. The copy skips the `perm:*` wildcard that `matches()` accepts. It also adds every role's Employee grants on its own assumption, which is not what canEver does. So this test can disagree with the permission model it is meant to check, in both directions. Fix: drop the copy. Call `setGrants(modules)` and check `canEver({ assignments: [{ role }, { role: "Employee" }], ... }, permission)` from @amax/auth, the way apps/web/tests/admin/it-admin.test.ts already does.

The test only checks that the role holds the permission the tool declares. It does not check the permission for the step the card shows. fi2 shows Finance approving a claim the manager already approved. In `modules/expenses/server/decide.ts:17`, that step needs `expenses:approve-finance`. But `approve_expense` declares `expenses:approve`, and every role holds that through OWN (`modules/expenses/module.ts:9`). So the fi2 row passes no matter what Finance can do. The same gap applies to any tool whose service picks a stricter permission per step. Fix: let a card name the permission for its step, e.g. `{ tool: "approve_expense", permission: "expenses:approve-finance" }`, check that permission, and add a rejecting row such as Engineer at the Finance step of approve_expense.

This is an instance fix. Last round's finding said the gap covers every tool whose service picks a stricter permission per step, but `step` was added only to fi2. hr1 has the same gap. The card shows HR approving Sophie Nguyen's leave as HR, not as her manager. `chainFor` in modules/leave/server/scope.ts:36 grants that HR step only through `leave:admin`. `approve_leave` declares `leave:approve`, and PM, Engineer, Finance, Sales, Payroll and Leadership all hold that through MANAGE (modules/leave/module.ts:10, 27-32). So the hr1 row only proves that some role holds `leave:approve`. It says nothing about HR's step. The cause is that `step` is optional and nothing makes a card set it, so any new card on a step-dependent tool passes silently. Fix: set `step: "leave:admin"` on hr1. Then either derive the step permission from the tool's service, or keep a list of tools with step-dependent services (approve_expense, reject_expense, approve_leave and the other leave decide tools) and fail any card on those tools that has no `step`. Also add a rejecting row per step, e.g. Engineer at the HR step of approve_leave.

The new rejection test calls `holds("Engineer", "expenses:approve-finance")` directly and never goes through the card check that the fix added. It doesn't prove the fix works: delete `...(step ? [step] : [])` from the loop at line 25 and every test stays green. It also has only one row, where B2 asks for the named case plus two others. Fix: pull the per-card check into a function, such as `check(role, card)`, that both the passing rows and a rejecting table use. Feed it at least three cards whose tool permission the role holds but whose step it doesn't: Engineer on `{ tool: "approve_expense", step: "expenses:approve-finance" }`, PM on `{ tool: "approve_leave", step: "leave:admin" }`, and a third such as HR on the same expense step. Expect each one to be rejected.

This is still an instance fix. hr1 now sets `step: "leave:admin"`, and the rejecting rows go through the shared `check()`, so the named cases are covered. The root cause the last round named is still there: `step` stays optional in `Card` (queues.ts:3), and `check()` only tests a step when the card sets one. A card on a tool whose service checks a stricter permission at each step can leave `step` out and pass. That covers approve_leave and reject_leave, which reach the HR branch only through `leave:admin` (modules/leave/server/scope.ts:36), and approve_expense and reject_expense, whose Finance step needs `expenses:approve-finance`. In those cases the test only proves that the role holds the tool's broad permission (`leave:approve` comes through MANAGE for PM, Engineer, Finance and the other roles). Fix: in the test, keep one list of tools with step-dependent services (approve_leave, reject_leave, approve_expense, reject_expense). Make `check()` fail any card on those tools that has no `step`. Add rejecting rows for that case, e.g. `["HR", { tool: "approve_leave" }]` and `["Finance", { tool: "reject_expense" }]`, each expected to fail because the step is missing.

The new smoke check can pass when a file is not actually served. `curl -sf` without `-w '%{http_code}'` only fails on 4xx/5xx, so a 3xx counts as success. That breaks AC-2, which says the job must fail on anything other than 200. The container is also started without DATABASE_URL, which leaves `guarded` null in apps/web/proxy.ts:11. So the check runs in guest-preview mode, where the signed-out gate never runs. The deployed image is gated, and that gate is exactly what a signed-out visitor goes through. The step therefore does not test what the marketing page's visitors get: a proxy matcher change that stops excluding one of these files would redirect it to /signin in production, and CI would stay green. Fix: assert the exact status code for each file (`test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' …)" = 200`). Also run the smoke container with a DATABASE_URL/auth config so the gate is live, for example a throwaway postgres service container. A unit test of the matcher against these five paths would also work.

This change adds personal data that the retention and erasure rules never reach. (1) `time.entry.deleted_by` (migration 0003) holds the acting person's id, but it is in neither `subject` nor `fields` of the `time.entry` entry. The old blocker lesson was about `time.entry.logged_by`; this is the same class of defect. (2) `time.change_request.before` and `.proposed` are jsonb copies of the entry's free-text `note`. They are not in the change-request entry's `fields`, so anonymising leaves the note text in place. Fix: add `deleted_by` to the time.entry rule's `subject` and `fields`, and add `before` and `proposed` to the change_request rule's `fields`. Also extend check-module-standard so it also flags `*_by` columns added by `alter table` and jsonb columns that copy personal columns.

The new 'Continue as …' link renders `href={to}`. `to` only checks that `next` starts with '/' and not with '//', so `/\evil.example` passes, and browsers treat a backslash as a slash. Before this change, `to` was only passed to Auth.js `redirectTo`, which validates it against the base URL; this raw anchor has no such check. Fix: resolve `to` with `new URL(next, origin)` and keep it only when the origin matches, or reject any backslash.

credentialsSignIn revokes the browser's current session before it checks the new credentials. A failed sign-in therefore still ends a live session. Fix: sign in first, then revoke the session it replaced, for example in the Auth.js signIn callback or by comparing session stamps after success.

There are now two delete paths for an entry. `writeDelete` soft-deletes (sets `deleted_at` and `deleted_by`, and keeps the row, as the README says). The commit-draft `undo` still runs a hard `delete from time.entry`. The hard delete loses the row the README promises to keep, and it fails on the new `time.change_request.entry_id` foreign key whenever any request, open or closed, references the entry. Fix: make undo call `writeDelete` (or the same soft-delete SQL) and reuse its event.

The fix that makes the confirm card match the stored entry (`checkCard`, hoursBefore) runs only when the card is proposed. correctEntry and deleteEntry do not re-check when the write runs. The change-request path pins `revision` and refuses a moved entry, but these two tools don't. Fix: put `hoursBefore` (or the revision read at propose time) into the input and refuse the write in the service when the locked entry no longer matches.

`requestRows` applies `limit 200` across the whole tenant before `listRequests` filters by viewer, status or week. Any request outside the 200 newest silently disappears, and the result looks complete. This affects get_change_requests, the Team time 'Change requests' card, MyRequests and the 'Review change requests' suggestion. Fix: push the viewer, status and week filters into SQL and apply the limit after them, or say plainly when the list was cut off.

`reason(e)` puts the database driver's raw error message into each per-person result. That message reaches the done card, the model (the result is quoted to it) and the audit `after`. This is the raw-error leak that toolFailure and doneNote were fixed for, now on a new path. Fix: map known refusals (Error from decide/writeRemind) to their message, and replace anything else with a logged reference such as 'couldn't be done (ref …)'.

Applying a change request that moves an entry to another project skips the project-scope check that correct_time_entry runs (`fixedBy` → `mayFix(v, owner, newProjectId)`). The `whoFor` callback here only looks up names. So an approver who is in the week's chain through project A can move the owner's hours onto project B, which they don't approve. Fix: in `whoFor`, check `mayFix(viewerOf(ctx), entry.user_id, projectId)` (or reuse `fixedBy`). Do the same check in `proposeDecide`/`checked`, so chat shows no card for a move the approver can't make. Add a variant test: a move to a managed project, to an unmanaged project, and with no move.

AC-52 (ending the browser's earlier session on a switch) runs only in `credentialsSignIn`. The Microsoft/OIDC provider form calls `signIn` directly, so a sign-in through Entra from a sign-in tab that was already open leaves the replaced session row unrevoked. Fix: run the same `sessionStamp` + `endSwitchedSession` step in the provider action, or in the Auth.js signIn callback so every provider gets it.

The fix for the 200-row cap removed the limit but did not move the real filter into SQL. The SQL filters are now applied first, but 'who reviews it' still runs in JS: one `reviews()` call per row, each one querying `weekProjectIds`. The fetch has no bound at all, so get_change_requests with no status, or with a closed status, returns the tenant's whole history. That means one chain query per other person's request, and the full list goes into the model's context. The new test needs a 60 s timeout for only 250 rows. Fix: express the approver's scope in SQL (the week's project ids against the viewer's approvable projects, or `user_id = viewer`), then page the result with a limit and a cursor or `truncated` flag the caller can see.

The AC-52 variant test calls `config.events.signIn` with an Auth.js message it builds by hand (`account: { amax: after }`). It also passes `replaced` as a stub that returns `before`. That leaves the parts the fix depends on untested: Auth.js firing the event after `callbacks.signIn` puts `amax` on the Entra account, and `apps/web/auth.ts`'s `replaced = sessionStamp(await auth())` returning the browser's earlier session while a sign-in completes. If `auth()` there returned null or the new session, every case would still pass and no earlier session would be revoked. Fix: drive at least one real sign-in through the Auth.js handler (a credentials POST to /api/auth/callback/password carrying an earlier session cookie, and an Entra callback with a mocked token endpoint), and assert that the earlier session row ends.

`failureNote` assumes any plain `Error` with no `cause` was written by this module, and passes its message on to the done card, the model and the audit `after`. Infrastructure errors don't fit that assumption. postgres-js throws its connection errors (CONNECTION_CLOSED, CONNECTION_DESTROYED, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, ECONNRESET) as plain `Error` objects with only a `code` and no cause, and those messages include the database host and port. The rest of the app already has one rule for this: `toolFailure` in packages/ai/src/gateway.ts maps a failure to a fixed phrase by error name or code and never uses the message. This change adds a second, looser classifier, so the two can disagree (B4). Fix: send module refusals through a dedicated class, such as `ToolError` (which `card.ts` already uses) or `ValidationError`, and keep only the messages of those classes. Everything else, including a plain `Error`, should map to the reference note. Add a postgres-js-style connection error to the table test.

`KNOWN_UNNAMED` lets 15 existing columns through the new per-column retention check. Several hold personal data that erasure and anonymisation never reach: `notifications.preference.email`, `compliance.incident.notify_by`, `presales.activity.note`, `presales.stage_change.note`, `presales.suggestion.client_name` and `career.history.detail`. These columns predate this change. They are tracked only in a follow-ups note, and no change owns them. Fix: open a change per module to add the columns to its retention entries, then remove them from the list.

The last round's blocker is fixed for six named columns, but the same pattern has moved into `keep`. `compliance.evidence_bundle.contents` is personal data: `modules/compliance/server/evidence.ts:28` writes `generatedBy: by(ctx)` and whatever each control's `build()` returns into it. The `keep` text itself says so and defers the problem to '070 follow-ups'. No change owns that follow-up, so erasure and anonymisation still never reach this column. That is exactly what the previous blocker objected to with `KNOWN_UNNAMED`. `keep` was added to the standard for columns with no person in them, and this column has one. Fix: either keep the person out of the signed payload (sign a pseudonymous reference instead), or open a change that owns re-signing or tombstoning the bundle on erasure. Until then, do not list `contents` as safe to keep.

The new per-column check only covers columns whose names look personal, plus json/jsonb columns, and only inside tables that already have a personal-named column. It misses the class this round fixed by hand. Free-text columns such as `detail`, `description`, `summary`, `body` and `reason` don't match `PERSONAL`, which is why `career.history.detail`, `it_access.change.detail`, `presales.*.note` and `delivery.deployment.note` had to be added manually. It also skips a jsonb column in a table whose only person column is a pseudonymous `user_id`, even though the comment says jsonb 'can carry a copy of one'. Fix: check every text and json column of any table that has a retention entry or a `user_id`/`person_id`, and require it to appear in `fields`, `subject`, `subjectName` or `keep`. Add these cases to the ac7-config table.

This is still an instance fix of the round-1 B2 finding. The test now builds real cookies, but it still calls `config.events.signIn` by hand with an Auth.js message it constructs itself (`account: { amax }` / `user: { amax }`). Two things the fix depends on remain unexercised. First, that Auth.js fires `events.signIn` after `callbacks.signIn` has put `amax` on the Entra account. Second, that `apps/web/auth.ts`'s `replaced` (`cookies()` from next/headers) still sees the earlier session cookie at that moment, both in the credentials server action and in the `/api/auth/callback` route. If either is wrong, every case still passes and no session is revoked. Fix: drive at least one real sign-in through the Auth.js handler. For example, POST to `/api/auth/callback/password` with an earlier session cookie, and run an Entra callback against a mocked token endpoint. Then assert that the earlier session row has ended.

An unknown `before` cursor reads as the end of the list. The filter `(c.created_at, c.id) < (select … where b.id = ${f.before})` compares against NULL when the id doesn't exist, isn't visible under RLS, or was garbled by the model. No row matches, and `pageRequests` returns `{ requests: [], truncated: false }`, which says 'no older requests'. Fix: look the cursor row up first, and refuse with a ValidationError ('unknown before cursor') when it is missing, instead of returning an empty, complete page.

`failureNote` is still a second classifier of which errors are safe to show, and it disagrees with the rest of the app. `packages/api/src/rest.ts:18-20` treats `ToolError`, `ForbiddenError`, `ScopeError` and `ValidationError` as user-facing. Bulk accepts a new `Refusal` class instead, and it drops `ToolError` (which this module's own `refuse` in card.ts throws) and `ForbiddenError`. The fix the finding asked for was to use the existing classes, `ToolError` or `ValidationError`. Fix: throw `ToolError` / `ValidationError` from `decide` and `writeRemind`, delete `Refusal`, and use one shared predicate in both places.

The compliance blocker is fixed for `evidence_bundle.contents`, but `keep` still marks a column as safe even though it can hold a person. `delivery.proposal.meta` is kept as 'front matter … its owner is owner_name'. But the sync service accepts `meta: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (services.ts:203) and stores whatever the repo's front matter has (services.ts:273-279). Nothing stops an owner, author or reviewer key from landing there, so erasure and anonymisation never reach it. Fix: either reduce `meta` to a fixed list of keys with no person in them (sha, pr, verdict, withdrawn) before storing it, or move `meta` from `keep` to `fields`.

`bundleState` treats any bundle whose contents is `{}` as anonymised and returns `signatureValid: null`. Nothing records that an anonymise actually ran. So a bundle tampered to `{}` now reads as 'anonymised' instead of 'tampered'. That is evidence loss passed off as a known state. Fix: decide 'anonymised' from a marker the retention engine writes (for example `generated_by` anonymised, or an anonymised_at or audit entry). Report `{}` contents without that marker as signature invalid. Add the tamper-to-{} case to the registers test.

This round made `userFacing` the app's single rule for which errors a caller may read. But the new refusal `guardShown` throws a plain `Error`, so `userFacing` rejects it. The REST API (rest.ts:18) turns it into a 500 'internal' with a reference. Bulk and other reporters hide its message the same way. The same applies to the new plain `Error`s in the suggestion undo (suggestions.ts: 'that entry is already gone' / 'that week was submitted since'). Fix: throw these through `refuse(...)` from card.ts, which throws `ToolError(…, 'invalid_input')`, and assert the REST status in the test.

Partly fixed. The new e2e drives the real credentials server action, `cookies()` and the signIn event. The Entra path is still only tested by calling `config.events.signIn` with a hand-built `account: { amax }`. Nothing proves two things: that Auth.js passes the same `account` object to `events.signIn` after `callbacks.signIn` mutates it (authjs.ts:120), and that `cookies()` in the `/api/auth/callback/<entra>` route handler still sees the earlier session cookie. If either is wrong, every test passes and an Entra switch leaves the old session alive. Fix: run one Entra callback through the Auth.js handler against a mocked token/userinfo endpoint, with an earlier session cookie, and assert that the earlier session row has ended.

The round-2 finding asked for a check on every text and json column of a table about people. This fix only extends a list of column names (`FREE_TEXT`), so it is an instance fix. Any free-text column whose name is not on the list still passes: `title`, `subject`, `content`, `label`, `topic`, `outcome`, `memo`. Examples already in the repo are a sales task's `title` and an incident's `title`, both of which people write names into. The previous finding also asked to cover tables that have a retention entry but whose person columns are not named like personal columns; `aboutPeople` still leaves those out. Fix: in a table that has a retention entry or a person/user id, use the column type (`text`, `varchar`, `character varying`, `json`, `jsonb`, `text[]`) and require each such column to appear in fields, subject, subjectName or keep. Add `title text` and `varchar` cases to the ac7-config table.

Review round 4 fixed one case: the card-mismatch refusal in the correct/delete services now throws a ToolError, so `userFacing` lets the REST API answer 400 and the bulk card shows the text. Other refusals added in this change still throw a plain `Error`, so `userFacing` is false. REST then answers 500 `internal` with only a reference, and the guidance text is lost. Affected: `guardFixable` (week submitted, or approved and locked), `guardLock`/`lockRefusal` (guards.ts:31), `guardDayTotal` ('more than 24 h', guards.ts:41), `writeCorrection` ('no project X', correct.ts:37), `requestChange` (week is draft; an open request already exists; request.ts:34-37), `decideRequest` (request already decided; entry changed since; decide-request.ts:24-26,65), and `writeReopen` (reopen.ts:11). Fix: throw these as `ToolError(..., "invalid_input")`, like `refuse()` and `decide()`/`writeRemind` already do. Extend the round-4 `userFacing` test to these refusals.

This change adds jsonb columns that code reads for logic to retention `fields`: `delivery.proposal.meta`, `it_access.change.detail` and `career.history.detail`. When a row is anonymised, `applyRule` replaces a jsonb value with `'{}'` (packages/core/src/privacy/apply.ts:15). `delivery.proposal.meta` holds the `withdrawn` flag that `ACTIVE` filters on (queries.ts:59), plus the sha, pr and verdict that the sync fingerprints. `it_access.change.detail` holds `products`, `skuIds` and `externalUserId`, which the queued-change runner dereferences (apply.ts:26 `c.detail.products.join`). Fix: anonymise only the personal keys inside these documents, or move the personal text into its own column that retention can null. If the structure has no person in it, list the column under `keep` with the reason.

Change requests are closed in only one case: `submitWeek` completes requests in status 'reopened'. If the week is reopened by an Admin's `reopen_week`, or sent back by `reject_week`, its pending and needs_info requests stay open. The owner then fixes the entry directly, which bumps its revision. The request still sits on Team time and in the 'Review change requests' suggestion, and `apply` refuses it as stale. The approver can only decline it, and the owner's 'Change requested' notice stays up. Fix: when a week leaves submitted or approved through any path, close or cancel its open requests in the same transaction and emit `changeDecided`/`changeCompleted`. Add a test over reopen_week, reject_week and a decide-reopen.

The new table `time.setting` has a personal column `updated_by` (it holds the acting person's id or name, written by `by(ctx)`). `modules/time/module.ts` has no 032 retention entry for `time.setting`. The module standard requires a retention entry for every personal-data table, and `*_by` columns are named as personal. Without one, erasure requests and legal holds never reach the person who last changed the rules. Fix: add a retention entry with `updated_by` in `subject` and `fields`, or keep the row with a stated reason.

`reaches(v, entity)` is true when *any* of the viewer's role assignments is unscoped or covers the entity. It does not check the assignment that grants `time:approve`. The manager path in `chainFor` (and its copy in `hours-scope.ts:22`) is `canEver(time:approve) && reaches(...)`. So a manager whose approving role is scoped to entity A still reaches a report in entity B through an unscoped base role such as Employee. The 071 entity narrowing is bypassed for managers. Fix: only count assignments whose role grants `time:approve` (or Admin), and add that case to the entity-scope test.

A partial time read now sets `timeIncomplete` and flags people `overtime-unknown`. A time read that did not happen at all does neither. Three cases all go through `none(...)`: a drafter without `time:totals` (ForbiddenError), a system draft, and a viewerless context. Each returns empty hours with `unreadable` empty, so the run shows no warning chip and no per-person flag. "Could not ask" reads the same as "no overtime", and HR or Finance approve a run that silently left out approved overtime. Fix: in these branches, mark every person in `userIds` unreadable (or set `timeIncomplete`).

The replay check compares project, day, hours and billable, but not `note`, which is part of the input. A retry with the same `clientRef` and a different note returns `replayed: true` instead of the refusal that README and AC-8 promise ("other input is refused"). The new note is silently dropped. The idempotency test has no note case. Fix: compare the stored note (and `agent`) too, and add the case to the test table.

The repeated-push filter covers only GitHub's `distinct` flag. Azure DevOps `git.push` events for a commit already pushed on another branch still pass through. Each push runs `draftCommitTime` again (a second activity line and a second pending suggestion), because time's handler dedups only commits that are already *logged*. Fix: dedup per commit id for every provider, for example in `draftCommitTime` or by checking time's pending suggestions by `source_ref`.

`hoursVisibleTo` writes Time's visibility rule a second time, and its project-manager path is wider than `seesWeek`. It grants the whole person for the whole range if they have any hours on a managed project in that range. Time's own reads (`seesWeek`, `weekTotals`, `weeklyHours`) grant only the weeks that contain hours on that project. This breaks the reports README's own rule that a report is 'never wider than the source modules'. Fix: in the PM path, return only the hours in weeks that `seesWeek` lets the viewer see, for example by keying visibility on user and week. Don't keep a separate month-wide rule.

The new entry-rule refusals are thrown as plain `Error`: `allocationRefusal` and `dateRefusal` in `logEntry`, `writeCorrection`, `guardOwnDate` (correct.ts) and `requestChange` (request.ts). They have no `code` and no `retryable: false`. `userFacing()` (packages/mcp/src/registry.ts:23) rejects them, so REST and other reporters show an 'internal' error and hide the message, including its list of allowed projects. The same class was fixed for `guardShown` in 070. Fix: throw `ToolError(..., 'invalid_input')`, or set `retryable: false`, wherever a rule refuses.

hoursVisibleTo now uses Time's seesWeek, but it works out each week's project set again, and differently. It only counts entries whose day is inside the report range (`e.day between from and to`). Time's own reads (contracts.ts `weekProjects`, team.ts) count every live entry of the week. So when a week crosses the range boundary, a PM's visibility differs between Time and Reports. Fix: build the project list per week_id over the whole week, the same way as `weekProjects` (or share one helper), instead of only the entries in range.

The migration says the commit_draft key is 'race-safe' (one draft per person and commit). ingest-ac2.test.ts only replays pushes one after another. No test runs two ingests of the same commit at the same time, for example a GitHub and an Azure DevOps delivery in parallel through Promise.all on separate sessions, and then checks for exactly one draft and one activity line. Fix: add that concurrent case.

The previous round's finding was about a week that crosses the edge of the report range. hoursVisibleTo must count every live entry of that week, as Time's weekProjects does, and not only the entries inside the range. The fix in hours-scope.ts handles this (the class fix is in place), but no test covers it. Every case here uses the range 2026-10-01..2026-10-31 and days in W42 and W44, which sit wholly inside the range. If the old `e.day between from and to` filter came back, every case would still pass. The test also seeds its CON entry with `.catch(() => undefined)`. If that log fails, the W44 'only Contoso Portal' case still returns false, because the week then has no projects, so that case proves nothing. Fix: add a case for a week split by the range edge. Log Fleet Tracker hours for Kasun on a day just before `from` and Contoso hours just after it, in the same ISO week. Assert that Nimal sees the in-range day. Drop the swallowed catch so a failed seed fails the test.

Under 071 a PM can see someone's hours only for the weeks that hold hours on a project the PM approves (`hoursVisibleTo`). `loadInputs` still counts that person as soon as any hours are visible (`hours.has(p.userId)`). Their available hours cover the whole month, but logged and billable hours come only from the visible weeks. The hidden weeks therefore count as zero hours, and the report shows a lower utilisation as if it were that person's real figure. It also lowers the team figure. Fix: when the viewer can see only some of a person's weeks in the range, mark the row as partial or not visible (as the leave case does with 'Leave not visible to you') and leave it out of the team figure. Or limit the PM's view to people whose whole range they can see.

071 limits every Admin act on other people's time to the owner's legal entity (`adminOver`, `inEntity`). `setSettings` checks only `action: "time:admin"`. `can()` with no `legalEntityId` ignores `legalEntityIds`, so an Admin scoped to one entity can still change the tenant's entry rules. Those rules then refuse logs for people in every other entity. Fix: refuse the write unless the caller holds `time:admin` on an assignment with no entity scope (`legalEntityIds === null`). Do the same in `proposeSettings` so no chat card is shown, and add a test with an entity-scoped Admin.

071 narrows who reviews a request by the owner's legal entity only in `reviews()`. `scopeSql` stays the wider pre-071 rule (comment at line 63). `get_change_requests` takes `PAGE` rows by that wider SQL scope and filters them after the limit, so it no longer pages in SQL by the real scope (the 070 fix). For an entity-scoped approver, `can(v,'time:approve')` without an entity is true, so the SQL fetches every request in the tenant, and a page can be empty or short while `truncated` is true. Fix: put the owner's entity into `scopeSql` (join `auth.user` and filter on `legal_entity_id` against the viewer's assignments for `time:approve`) so the SQL and `chainFor` stay the same rule.

`logOnce` checks for a replay outside the `logTime` service, in its own read. So when a replay matches, `log_time` returns a value without reaching its declared service at all. Chat counts writes on confirm, and `packages/chat/src/engine.ts:304-305` closes an ok run with `writes === 0` as unknown ("couldn't confirm what it changed"). The `log_time` input schema offers `clientRef` to chat as well, so a confirmed card whose ref is already logged reads as unknown, not done. The `source_taken` fallback path does reach the service once, so the two replay paths end differently. Fix: do the lookup inside `logTime`'s `run`, in its transaction, and return the existing entry as the service result (one keyed call). Or keep `clientRef` out of the chat path.

An hour copied with a `week_id` but with no `reports.week_status` row is counted as a draft and dropped. That happens for any week submitted or approved before 072 was deployed: migration 0003 does not backfill `week_status`, and later events still write `week_id` into rows of those weeks. A correction raises the revision, so the upsert in `recordHours` sets `week_id` on a pre-072 row. An Admin's locked log into an old approved week inserts a new row that has a `week_id`. In both cases the left join gives `s.status` null, and the hours disappear, while the same week's other rows (`week_id` null) still count. An unknown status is being read as 'not submitted'. Fix: backfill `reports.week_status` from `time.week` in the migration (or seed it through Time's contract), and treat a `week_id` with no status row as unknown, not as a draft.

Weekly utilisation is computed twice, and the two copies disagree. `get_my_week` uses `hoursOf(sums)`, which is rounded to 0.1 h, and counts a sent-back week's hours. `get_week_utilisation` uses exact sums and counts 0 for a rejected week (D4). Fix: have `myWeek` take its hours, target and % from the same function `weekUtilisation` uses.

`people` is built from `teamWeek` rows, and those exist only where a `time.week` row exists. Someone who logged nothing in the week is missing from the result, not shown at 0%. The tool description then tells chat that a missing person is 'someone you may not see', so 'nothing logged' is reported as 'not visible'. Fix: list the people the viewer may see (for example, through hr/allocations or the same scope) and show those with no week at 0 h, with every working day so far as missing.

Leave is read through `approvedLeave` as the viewer. For a person whose leave the viewer may not see, the result looks like 'no leave'. Their leave days are then listed in `missingDays`, and the target is not adjusted, with no mark that leave was unreadable. Reports handles the same case with 'Leave not visible to you'. Fix: tell 'not visible' apart from 'no leave' (for example, `leaveVisible: false` on the row), and leave the leave days out of `missingDays` when leave can't be read.

`reaches` is a second, looser copy of Time's entity rule. It passes when any of the viewer's role assignments covers the entity, not the assignment that grants `time:approve`. Time's `chainFor` uses `approvesIn(v, entity)`: an approving role in the owner's entity. A manager whose approving role is scoped to another entity, but who holds an unscoped non-approving role (Engineer), is still notified. Fix: check `can(v, permission, { legalEntityId: entity })` (or reuse Time's rule) for managers and for the Admin fallback.

Time now imports `@amax/leave/contracts` statically, but Leave is not a declared dependency (Time's README still says Leave is 'not wired yet'). It also checks whether Leave is there with `to_regclass('leave.request')` instead of `hasModule('leave')`. The module standard says optional integrations check `hasModule` and that removing a module's folder leaves the app building. Fix: declare Leave as an optional integration, gate the call on `hasModule('leave')`, and add the with/without-Leave test.

The `time.target` retention entry has `updated_by` in `subject` and `action: "delete"`. An erasure or hold for the Admin who set a target therefore deletes another person's target row. The 7-year purge also deletes the target of an active person who hasn't changed it since. Either way the person goes back to 40 h without anyone deciding it. The sibling `time.setting` entry anonymises. Fix: use `action: "anonymise"`, so erasing the actor nulls `updated_by` and keeps `hours`.

This is an instance fix: the finding wasn't fixed, only re-described. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `teamWeek` rows, and both need a `time.week` row. So someone who logged nothing in the week is still left out instead of shown at 0 h with every working day so far missing. The tool description now says a missing person 'has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see'. That still mixes up 'logged nothing' and 'not visible', and `below` can never return the person who is furthest below. Fix: list the people the viewer may see (the same scope as `hoursVisibleTo`/teamWeek, over hr people). Show those with no week at 0 h, status null and missingDays set to every working day before today.

Half of the previous finding is still open. Time still imports `@amax/leave/contracts` statically, and it still decides whether Leave is installed with `to_regclass('leave.request')` instead of `hasModule('leave')`. Only the README changed. A switched-off Leave keeps its tables, so Time still reads and adjusts by leave. The new 'without Leave' test drops the `leave` schema. That isn't the module being switched off, so it never covers the `hasModule` path. Fix: gate `leaveIn` and the `leaveVisibleTo` check on `hasModule('leave')`. Test with `AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave` (or the registry without Leave), not by dropping the schema.

This is an instance fix. The backfill covers weeks that existed when the migration ran, but the query still reads a `week_id` with no `week_status` row as a draft. The previous finding asked for that case to be treated as unknown. A week can still lack a status row:
- a week submitted between the migration and the 072 handlers going live (the event is consumed by a worker with no `week_status` handler);
- a week whose status event was dead-lettered.
In both cases the week's hours that carry a `week_id` are silently dropped, while its rows with a null `week_id` still count. Fix: when a row has a `week_id` and no status row, report it as unknown (or flag the person's figure as incomplete) instead of excluding it as a draft.

The fix for the missing-status major is proven by one case only: an applied change request on W42. The finding named at least two paths that write a `week_id` into an old week's rows: a correction that raises the revision, and an Admin's locked log into an old approved week. There is also an approved week, as well as a submitted one. Fix: add a table-driven test over these variants that fails without migration 0004.

Reports' migration reads `time.week` directly. The standard says a module's migrations touch only its own schema, and cross-module reads go through the owner's contract. This ties Reports' schema to Time's table layout and gets around Time's data scope. Fix: seed `reports.week_status` through a Time contract read run as a system job (for example a one-off workflow or the handler's first run), not from SQL against another schema.

Instance fix, and in fact not a fix: someone with no timesheet that week is still left out of the result. The change only rewrites the tool description, which now tells chat that a missing person 'has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see'. Chat still can't tell 'logged nothing' from 'not visible'. `weekUtilisation` still builds `people` only from `myWeek` (when `mine.status` is set) and `teamWeek` rows, so the viewer is dropped too when they have no week. Fix: list every person the viewer may see (the same 071 scope `teamWeek` applies, through hr/allocations). Show those with no `time.week` row at 0 h, against their target, with every working day so far in `missingDays`.

Instance fix. This round changed only the tool description (mcp-utilisation.ts:10) and the README, and now both document the defect. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `teamWeek` rows, and both need a `time.week` row. Anyone who logged nothing that week is left out, including the viewer. `below` therefore can never return the person who is furthest below target. The description tells chat to answer 'either has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see', which still merges 'logged nothing' with 'not visible'. Fix: list every person the viewer may see (the same 071 scope `teamWeek`/`hoursVisibleTo` applies, over hr people). Show anyone without a week at 0 h with status null, against their target, with every working day before today in `missingDays`.

Still open. Whether Leave is present is decided by `to_regclass('leave.request')`, not by whether the module is installed. The new `leaveVisible` flag (line 63) and the leave adjustment both hang off that check. The new no-Leave test only covers a database where Leave was never migrated. It doesn't cover the real case: Leave switched off with `AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave` on a database that already has its tables. Fix: gate `leaveIn` and the `leaveVisibleTo` check on the installed-module registry, not on the table existing, and test with Leave's tables present but the module disabled.

The fix removes 'no status = draft' only when Time answers. If Time can't be asked (`installed(tx,'time.week')` is false), `fromTime` is an empty Map. If Time no longer has the week id (purged or erased week), the id is missing from the result. In both cases `counts` returns false and the hours are dropped exactly as a draft would be, with nothing on the row or the team figure to say so. 'Could not ask' still reads as 'not counted'. Fix: when a row has a `week_id` and neither the local copy nor Time gives a status, flag that person's figure as incomplete/unknown (as Reports does with 'Leave not visible'). Don't silently exclude the row.

The variant test has two cases, and the second does not drive the real path: it plants the missing-status state with a hand `delete from reports.week_status`. The previous finding named an Admin's locked log into an old approved week, and that variant is still missing. The test also has no case for Time not answering (no status from either source). Fix: add the locked-log variant, and a case where the status is missing because the event wasn't consumed (for example, emit the approval with the Reports handler absent), not deleted by hand.

Instance fix, and the same defect is still open. This round again changed only the tool description (mcp-utilisation.ts:10) and the README. Both now document the gap instead of closing it. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `team.rows`, and both need a `time.week` row. Anyone who logged nothing that week is left out, including the viewer. So `below` can never return the person who is furthest below target. The description tells chat that a missing person 'either has no timesheet that week or isn't someone you may see', which still treats 'logged nothing' and 'not visible' as one answer. Fix: list every person the viewer may see. Use the same 071 scope that `teamWeek`/`seesWeek` apply, over hr people, plus the viewer. Show anyone without a week at 0 h with status null, against their target, with every working day before today in `missingDays`. Add a variant test: the viewer with no week, a report with no week, and a PM-visible person with no week.

The round-3 fix now also counts `hoursIncomplete` rows in `team.leftOut`. Two places that explain `leftOut` still give only the old reason. The lede at view.ts:44 says '... left out of the team figure: their leave isn't visible to you', and the contract doc at contracts.ts:26 says '`leftOut` had leave the viewer can't see'. A person left out because their timesheet status is unknown is therefore explained as hidden leave. Fix: count the two reasons apart (for example `leftOut` and `statusUnknown`, or a per-reason breakdown), give the matching sentence in the lede and the CSV/Team row, and update the contract doc.

The 'status unknown → incomplete' fix (inputs.ts unknownFor) is proven by one case, and that case plants an orphan `week_id` by hand in `reports.logged_hours`. The fix covers two variants that real paths can reach, and neither is tested. (1) Time switched off (`hasModule('time', …)` false): set `setInstalledModules` without 'time' on a database whose copied hours carry week ids that have no status row. Every such person must come back `hoursIncomplete`, not dropped. (2) A week the viewer may not see in Time while the copied hour is still visible, or a week removed through Time's own retention or erasure path. Fix: make this a table-driven test with at least the Time-off case and one more case driven through a real path, beside the planted one.

`unknownFor` is one set of people built from every hour that `loadInputs` reads, and `getReport` loads 12 months of hours so it can draw the trend (`view.ts:38`). `utilisationOf(inputs, range)` treats `inputs.hoursUnknown` as if it belonged to the month asked for, but it covers the whole year. So one week with an unknown status in any of those 12 months marks the person `hoursIncomplete` in the current month's table (null %, out of the team figure) and in every trend month too. It also adds a row for someone who has no hours in the month at all (`figures.ts` filter `inputs.hoursUnknown.has(p.userId) || …`). Fix: key the unknown set by person and day, or by person and week (for example keep the unknown rows' days), and in `utilisationOf`/`personFigures` mark a person incomplete only when an unknown-status hour falls inside `range`. Add cases where the unknown week is outside the month and in another trend month.

The newest-wins guard (`where reports.week_status.as_of < excluded.as_of`) orders a week's events by `core.event.created_at`. That column defaults to `now()`, which is the start time of the emitting transaction, not its commit order. A transaction that started earlier but locked the week and committed later (for example a reopen that waited on the approve's row lock) gets the older timestamp. Its status is then refused, and Reports keeps the stale one. No test runs two real transactions on the same week. Fix: order by something that follows commit order for the week (a per-week sequence or revision from Time carried in the payload, or `clock_timestamp()` taken after the week's row lock). Add a two-session test where the transaction that starts first commits last.

`below` and the lowest-first sort both use the raw `utilisation`, which ignores leave, even when a leave-adjusted `adjustedUtilisation` was worked out for that row. So 'Who is below 80% this week?' lists people whose only shortfall is approved leave. Fix: filter and sort on `adjustedUtilisation ?? utilisation`, or state in the tool's contract and description that `below` ignores leave. Add a table-driven case: no leave, leave that takes someone above the threshold, and leave the viewer can't see.

Migration 0007 adds two personal-data tables, but neither has a retention entry. `time.reminder` stores `user_id`, `sent_by` (a `*_by` column), `sender_name` (a name column with no id beside it) and the sender's free-text `message`. `time.project_reminder` stores `updated_by`. Requests, holds and erasure find rows only through `subject` and `subjectName`, so they never reach these rows. Add an entry for `time.reminder` with subject ["user_id","sent_by"], subjectName ["sender_name"] and fields ["message","sent_by","sender_name"]. Add an entry for `time.project_reminder` with subject and fields ["updated_by"].

`onProjects` reads the allocations and HR schemas directly with raw SQL (`allocations.allocation a join hr.person p`). architecture.md says cross-module reads go through the owning module's contract functions, which apply the caller's data scope. This read skips the boundary and the scope, and `check:graph` can't see it because no import is involved. `expectedBy`/`expectedIn` feed Team time, reminders, utilisation and Not started. Read allocations through `@amax/allocations/contracts` and persons through `@amax/hr/contracts`, as capacity.ts already does.

`claimChoice` claims the other options' keys as cancelled, but it never checks that this option is still pending, and it doesn't claim this option's own key under the lock. When two options are confirmed at once, each can cancel the other: A commits its claim on B; B then takes the lock, still sees A in pending, claims A's key as cancelled and settles it. Both runs then hit CancelledByKeyError. The person confirmed an option and is told it was cancelled. The race test only asserts `ran.length <= 1`, so it stays green when nothing ran. Fix: under the lock, refuse when this action is already decided or its own key is claimed, and claim this option's key as in-flight before cancelling the others. Then assert exactly one write.

`claimKey(...).catch(() => ({ done: null }))` turns a failed claim, such as a DB error, into 'another option already ran'. `confirmCard` then records `not_chosen` and throws the cancelled outcome. A claim that could not be made must surface as an error or retry, never as a decision.

Applying an 'add' request returns before the `mayMove` project check, and `add()` in decide-request.ts doesn't check the project either. `logEntry` with `requestId` also skips `assertCan`. A reviewer who is in the week's chain through project A can therefore log hours on project B, which they don't approve. On an approved week this is also a locked change. This is the same class as the earlier change-request project-scope lesson. Require `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId })` for the proposed project, or the manager or Admin chain, in both the card and the service.

`remindNotStarted` wraps each person in `tx.transaction(...)` but never catches the error. One failure therefore aborts the whole remind_weeks service, including the weeks already reminded, instead of producing a 'failed' row. The week loop above catches per person; this second path doesn't. Wrap it in try/catch and push `{ status: 'failed', note: failureNote(e) }`.

The new sent-back card shows a record (the rejected week, with who sent it back and why) but has no `PinButton`. Its Ask amax buttons carry a pin, but the card itself can't be pinned. Add `<PinButton inline pin={pin} />`.

The new project-row pins name the project by name: `get_team_week {week, project: p.name}` here, and `get_timesheet {weekId, project: n}` in SheetPage.tsx. Both tools resolve by a case-insensitive name match, so a renamed project makes the pin resolve to null. 059 says a record is pinned by its UUID. Pass `projectId` and resolve by id.

The new personal-data tables have no retention entries. `time.reminder` holds `sent_by`, `sender_name` (a name), `message` and `user_id`. `time.project_reminder` holds `updated_by`. module.ts `retention` gains no entry for either, which breaks the module standard (032): every personal-data table needs an entry with `subject` / `subjectName`. Erasure, legal holds and the purge never reach these rows. Fix: add entries. For `time.reminder`, use subject [user_id, sent_by] and subjectName [sender_name], with fields [message, sent_by, sender_name]. For `time.project_reminder`, use subject/fields [updated_by].

Instance fix of the round-1 'pin keyed on a name' finding (R3/059). ThisWeek and SheetPage now pin project rows by `projectId`, but this file is in the diff and was missed. The project rows of My timesheet still pin `get_timesheet { week, project: <name> }`, and `getTimesheet` resolves that by a name match. `MyRow` carries no project id, so the page can't pass one. Fix: add `projectId` to `MyRow` in my.ts and pin `{ week: m.key, projectId }`. Extend pin-by-id.test.ts to cover the own-week path.

`onProjects` now reads allocations through `listAllocations`, which returns `{ rows, hidden }`, and keeps only `rows`. People the reader's HR scope can't see are dropped without a trace. The code treats them as 'not allocated', so 'could not see' reads as 'nothing there'. Before this change the raw SQL counted them. `expectedBy`, which feeds Not started, remind_missing and utilisation, now leaves them out with no signal. Fix: surface `hidden` (for example, a 'N people on your projects could not be checked' note on the card or grid), or resolve a manager's own projects through a contract read that is scoped to project management rather than HR visibility.

`mayAddOn` is a second rule for the same question `mayFix` and `mayMove` answer: may this viewer put the owner's hours on project P in a locked week? The two can disagree. `mayFix` lets in anyone with `time:log` scoped to the owner in their entity; `mayAddOn` lets in only the owner's direct manager who also approves in that entity. Applying a 'move to P' request and an 'add on P' request therefore get different answers for the same viewer, owner and project. Fix: derive one predicate from the other (for example, `mayAddOn = (v, owner, p, e) => mayFix(v, owner, p, e)` plus the manager clause, if the manager clause is the intended rule for both). Use it from mayMove too.

This is an instance fix of the 'pin keyed on a name' finding. `get_timesheet` takes `projectId`, but it turns the id back into the project's current name and filters by name again: `own` uses `r.projectName === project`, and `projectRow` uses `e.projectName === project`. That happens even though `EntryLine` now carries `projectId`. A name is not unique. `projectNames` (`listProjectRefs`) also returns only active projects, so the id of a closed project's row resolves to null even though the row is on the page. SheetPage also gets the pin's id by name (`cells.flatMap(...).find((p) => p.name === n)`), so rows that share a name get the first project's id. Filter entries and rows by `projectId` all the way through, and group SheetPage rows by id, not by name.

Two of this round's fixes ship without a test that drives them. (1) The B3 fix removes `.catch(() => ({ done: null }))` from `claimChoice`, but no test makes `claimKey` fail and asserts the confirm surfaces an error instead of a `not_chosen`/cancelled decision. (2) The B10 blocker fix in `expected.ts` (reads through the allocations and HR contracts) has no test showing that allocated-but-not-logged people are still expected for `expectedBy` and `expectedIn`. Add a table-driven test for each that fails without the fix.

The fix adds the manager clause in one place only, so there are still two rules that disagree about who may put the owner's hours on project P in a locked week. Applying a change request (adding or moving hours) now uses `mayPutOn`, which is `mayFix` plus 'the owner's manager who approves in that entity'. But `correct_time_entry` and its card still use plain `mayFix` (`fixedBy` at entry.ts:67, and card.ts:44). So a manager who doesn't approve P is refused a direct move to P but allowed the same move through a request. Fix: pick one rule and use it everywhere. Either use `mayPutOn` from `fixedBy` and card.ts too, or drop the manager clause from `mayPutOn`. Then add a table-driven test that runs both paths for the same viewer, owner and project.

I expect the new Not started test to fail no matter what the fix does. It asserts that Dinesh's row has `status: "sent"`, but `remindNotStarted` only ever pushes `status: "done"` for a successful reminder (bulk.ts:44, and :68 for weeks). So the round-1 per-person failure fix has no passing test that proves it. It also checks only one variant (one person failing in one Not started card), not a table. Fix: assert `status: "done"`, and make it table-driven, for example: the failing person first, the failing person last, and everyone failing. Each case should check the recorded rows.

The new early `return false` treats "this option is no longer in `pending`" as "a sibling beat it". That is not the only reason the option can be missing. If the same option is confirmed twice (double tap, or a retry while the first run is still going), the first attempt settles the option as confirmed and removes it from `pending`. The second attempt passed `lookupKey` before that settle, then reaches `claimChoice`, gets `false`, records `not_chosen`, and throws `NotPendingError("cancelled")`. Before this change, the sibling claims returned `cancelled`, the loop went on, and `withIdempotency` replayed the stored outcome. Fix: when the option is missing from `pending`, look up its own key (or its `decided` entry) and only return lost when a sibling's key holds a done/in-flight outcome. If its own key is settled, fall through so the replay path reports `already_done`. Add a test that confirms the same option twice at once and expects one write and two `done` outcomes, with no cancel.

The round-3 fix only covers the case where the same option was already settled as `confirmed`. Any other own decision (`unknown`, `failed`, `expired`) returns false. confirmCard then records `not_chosen`, calls `cancelled()` (whose settle overwrites `decided[id]` with `cancelled`) and tells the person nothing was changed. An `unknown` outcome means the write may have run, so it is reported as a clean cancel and the stored decision is rewritten. Fix: when the option is no longer pending, return lost only when `decided[action.id]` is `cancelled` (a sibling beat it). For any other own decision, fall through so `withIdempotency` (or a fresh `lookupKey`) reports the key's real outcome. Do not settle over it. Add cases for `unknown` and `failed` to the double-confirm test.

The new same-option double-confirm test says in its own comment that it does not force the interleaving the fix is for (attempt 2 passing `lookupKey` before attempt 1 settles). It also passes without the round-3 change, so it doesn't prove the fix (B2/B7). Fix: force the order. For example, hold a lock or delay attempt 1's settle (a trigger on `core.idempotency` or `chat.conversation`, or an injected hook) until attempt 2 has passed `lookupKey`. Then assert one write, two `done` outcomes and no `not_chosen` step. Also cover the case where the first attempt's decision is `unknown`.

Approved leave is read with a system job context (`contextFor.job`) and shown to the viewer, so Leave's visibility rule is skipped. 072 reads leave as the viewer and sets `leaveVisible: false` where Leave hides it (utilisation.ts:35, :69). This change adds four more copies that read it as a job: grid-context.ts ("On leave" cells on Team time), anomalies.ts `missingDays` (the approve card's "Check: missing …" leaves out leave days), reminders.ts `dayState` (the remind card says "skipped: on approved leave") and my-days.ts. Fix: read leave through `approvedLeave(tx, viewer, …)` and filter with `leaveVisibleTo`, in one shared helper. Where the viewer can't see a person's leave, show the day as unknown, never as leave. The same applies to `listPeople(tx, job, {})` for departments.

Round 3 gave remind_weeks and remind_missing a savepoint per person, so one failure fails only that person. The scheduled loops in `remindDaily` and `remindDrafts` were missed: they write every reminder in the service's single transaction. One person's failed insert rolls back the whole entity run. The step retries 3 times, then nobody in the entity is reminded. Fix: wrap each `writeDayReminder` and `recordReminder` in `tx.transaction`, record the failure, and continue. Add a variant test that makes the first person, the last person, and everyone fail.

`switchedOff` judges a person only by the projects they logged time on in the last 28 days. `expectedIn` also includes people who are only allocated (no entries). Their project switch is never checked, so a PM's switch-off doesn't reach them. Fix: include the person's allocated projects (through the allocations contract) in the projects that `switchedOff` considers.

`claimChoice` claims every sibling option's key as cancelled and records them as "Not chosen" before the chosen option runs. If the chosen write then fails for good (failed, or the input is refused), nothing was written, but every other option is already closed. The person can't pick the option that would have worked. The UI also keeps the siblings open, because it closes them only on done or cancelled. Fix: on a final failure, release the siblings (or claim them only after the write commits, inside the same keyed run), and test the failure path.

Stale invoice suggestions are withdrawn only inside the `invoiceDrafted` handler, so only when a newer draft replaces the old one. `draftFor` (modules/finance/server/drafts.ts:31-32) can also mark the open draft `superseded` and then return null with no event, when the new amount is 0. That happens when the only approved time for the contract is reopened or sent back. No handler runs, and the old draft's suggestion stays open with its old amount. Fix: withdraw the superseded draft's suggestion where the draft is superseded, with or without a new draft. Either emit an event for the supersede itself, or call the withdrawal from `draftFor`. Add a variant test for the zero-amount reopen.

`expectedBy` treats anyone with time or an allocation on a project the viewer manages (`managed.has(id)`) as expected, in any legal entity. The 071 rule for project approvers (`mayFix` / `mayPutOn`: `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId, ...inEntity(entity) })`) limits them to the owner's entity, so this is a second copy of the scope rule and the two disagree. `remind_missing`, `remind_weeks` through `notStartedIn`, Team time's Not started rows and the Not started rows in `get_week_utilisation` all read `expectedBy`, so they reach people the viewer's 071 scope excludes. Fix: in the managed branch, also require `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId, ...inEntity(entityOf(id)) })`, or reuse the chain or entity check. Add a test with a PM scoped to one entity and an out-of-entity person on the managed project.

`judgeCovered` lets a fork PR skip review completely. The only check on the named change is that its final round's head is an ancestor of the PR head. That is always true for any change already merged or archived on main, because the fork branches from main. The gate never checks three things. (1) The covering loop's final head comes after this change's commits, so the loop actually saw them. (2) The covering change sits on this PR's branch (touched by the PR, or its reviewed head not already in base). (3) The covering change's `## Verify` names this change, which AGENTS.md requires. It also ignores the covered change's own `review/` rounds, so a change whose own loop left an open blocker can switch to `covered-by` and hide it. AGENTS.md says a fork PR 'must carry a finished loop for every change it touches', and this breaks that. Fix: pass when the cover's reviewed head is not an ancestor of `--base`, and every commit that touches the covered change dir is an ancestor of that reviewed head (`git rev-list base..head -- <dir>`, each checked with `merge-base --is-ancestor <c> <coverHead>`). Also require the covered change's name under the cover's `## Verify`. Fail when the covered change's own rounds show an open blocker.

Test AC1/AC2 makes the bypass the expected result. It passes `103-stacked` against `101-cover`, which sits in base and was reviewed at a head from before 103's commits. No test covers a cover whose reviewed head comes before the covered change's commits, a cover whose loop finished before the PR's base, or a cover whose `## Verify` doesn't name the covered change. Each of these should fail. Add those cases as a variant table, and change the 'touched or not' case so the cover's loop actually reviews 103's commits.

Instance fix. Round 1 asked that every commit touching the covered change's dir be an ancestor of the cover's reviewed head. `loopProblem` uses `.some(...)`, so the check passes once any one commit is older than the cover's final pass. Commits made to the covered change after the covering loop finished are never reviewed and still pass. This diff also rewrites AGENTS.md to say "after at least one of this change's commits", which lowers the law to match the code instead of fixing the code. Fix: use `.every(...)` over `history(change.dir)`, keep the original AGENTS.md wording, and add a test where the cover's final pass sits between two 103-stacked commits. That case must fail.

`history(change.dir)` only lists commits under the single dir that `touchedChangeDirs` picked. When the PR touches both `.specclaw/changes/103-x/` and `.specclaw/changes/archive/103-x/`, the sorted diff makes the archive dir win. A change archived on the stacked branch then has a history of just the move commit and later ones. Its real commits under the active dir are left out. The gate then fails a correctly covered change with "final pass ran before any commit". It also ignores commits made before the move. Fix: run `rev-list` over both the active and archive paths for the change, and add a test where a covered change is archived on the branch after the cover's final pass.

The round-1 finding is only partly fixed. `history` lists only commits that touch the covered change's own `.specclaw/changes/<name>` directory. Code commits for a change usually touch `modules/…` and nothing under its change directory, so `loopProblem` never sees them. A code commit made after the covering loop's final pass therefore goes unreviewed and still passes. The `between` test only fails because its late commit also writes `103-stacked/notes.md`. Fix: check every commit in `base..head` that is not an ancestor of the cover's final head. Every such commit that touches anything outside `.specclaw/` must be owned by a self-reviewed change in the PR. Add a test case with a code-only late commit.

`ownedElsewhere` excuses a late commit on its subject line alone. It only checks that the subject names some other self-reviewed change in the PR. It never checks that the other change's loop reviewed that commit, i.e. that the owner's final head descends from the commit. `judgeEvidence` only asks that the owner's final head is in the PR, so neither loop ever saw the commit. On a fork PR the subject is text the contributor chooses. Fix: excuse the commit only when `isAncestor(commit.sha, finalRound(owner.rounds).head)`. Add a test where the owner's final pass comes before the excused commit; that case must fail.

`verifySection` takes the first `indexOf("## Verify")` anywhere in the file. That can be a prose mention, for example 078's own change.md line 8 "(073 `## Verify`)" or 074's AC text. The new `split(/^## (?!Verify)/m)` then ends the section at the next heading, so the real `## Verify` is never read. The covered-by name check and the blocker-stop check both read the wrong text. They fail a correct cover, or pass when the prose near the mention happens to name the change. Fix: anchor the match to a heading line (`/^## Verify[ \t]*$/m`). Add test cases where the cover's change.md mentions `## Verify` in its Problem text.

`commit()` ignores `git show`'s exit status and decides `recordsOnly` with `paths.every(...)`. An empty path list therefore reads as 'records only'. That covers a `git show` that failed (missing object in a shallow or partial clone) and a clean merge commit, whose `--cc --name-only` output lists no files. Either way a late commit is excused as records-only instead of being reported as unknown. `history` also ignores `rev-list`'s status, so a failure there produces the misleading `final pass ran before any … commit`. Fix: throw on a non-zero status, as `inBase` does. Treat an empty path list as not records-only, and list merge files with `-m --first-parent` or `--diff-merges=first-parent`.

[design] This fixes only the named case. `history(change.name)` runs `rev-list` limited to `.specclaw/changes/<name>` and `archive/<name>`, so the after-final-pass check only sees commits that also touch the change's records dir. AGENTS.md now says that a commit to the change after the final pass must touch only `.specclaw/`. A code-only commit for the covered change never touches its dir, so the gate never sees it. The `between` test passes only because its planted commit edits `103-stacked/notes.md` as well as `modules/demo/c.ts`. Fix: attribute commits to the change by their subject as well as by path. Every commit in `base..head` whose subject names the covered change (`specclaw(<name>)` / `[specclaw] <name>`), or that touches its dir, must be an ancestor of the cover's final head or be records-only. Add a test with a code-only `specclaw(103-stacked)` commit after the cover's final pass, and assert it fails.

`excused` lets through every merge commit after the cover's final pass, whatever the merge itself changes. `rev-list` lists the side branch's own commits separately. The merge commit does not appear there, yet it can carry its own edits (a conflict resolution, or `git merge --no-commit` followed by extra edits). No loop ever saw those edits. `commit()` already works out the merge's first-parent `paths` and then ignores them for merges. Fix: excuse a merge only when the merge's own edits (`git show --remerge-diff --name-only`, or `--cc`) are empty or touch only `.specclaw/`. Otherwise treat it like any other late commit. Add a fixture with such a merge and assert that it fails.

Round 4 found a major (B3) in `commit()`: an empty path list counted as 'records only', and `git show`/`rev-list` failures were ignored. The fix adds `paths.length > 0`, `must()` and `--diff-merges=first-parent` but ships no test. No branch in the table has a late merge commit, a late records-only commit (which should pass), or an empty commit (which should fail). Each fix would pass the tests with its line deleted. Add variant rows: a late `.specclaw/`-only commit → pass; a late empty commit (`--allow-empty`) → fail; a late clean merge of a side branch whose commit edits `modules/` → fail.

[design] `commit()` builds `recordsOnly` from `git show --name-only`. Rename detection is on by default, and for a rename `--name-only` prints only the new path. A commit that moves a code file into `.specclaw/` therefore looks records-only, even though it deletes that code from the module. Fix: pass `--no-renames` so both the old and the new path are listed.

The fix ships one hand-picked case (T2, T10, T1) through `syncSpecclaw` only. It needs a table-driven test over the variants: the named T26-before-T25, a ref-length case (T10 before T9), a reverse-ordered list, and an already-sorted control. The test also never drives the second caller of `desired`, the repo push path (`server/push.ts:87` → `unchanged`), which has its own fingerprint comparison. A regression there stays green.
